skills.name: office-pptx
skills.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx file is involved as input or output - create, read, edit, combine, or split presentations, decks, and slides. Trigger on 'deck', 'slides', 'presentation', 'PPT', 'PowerPoint', or a .pptx filename. If a .pptx needs to be opened, created, or modified, use this skill.
skills.instructions:
---
name: office-pptx
description: >- Use this skill any time a .pptx file is involved as input or output - create, read, edit, combine, or split presentations, decks, and slides. Trigger on 'deck', 'slides', 'presentation', 'PPT', 'PowerPoint', or a .pptx filename. If a .pptx needs to be opened, created, or modified, use this skill.
---
# PPTX | Situation | Section |
|-----------|---------|
| Read, check, or preview any deck | [Read](#read) to [Finish line](#finish-line) |
| An existing `.pptx` is the source | [Edit an existing deck](#edit-an-existing-deck) |
| A new deck | [Create a new deck](#create-a-new-deck) and [Design](#design) | New files come from PptxGenJS. The `office pptx` and `office` commands never
create a deck from nothing. They open one, change it, check it, and render
it. ## Setup The commands are on `PATH`, work from any directory, and take `--help`.
Run Python with `python3`; python-pptx, openpyxl, pandas, and markitdown
are installed for it. PptxGenJS is installed globally, so
`require("pptxgenjs")` works from any folder. LibreOffice (`soffice`)
renders the previews with a fixed profile under `~/.cache/officekit`.
Previews use the fonts `fc-list` shows; `office pptx check-fonts` names the
substitute for a font the box does not have. ## Read ```bash
python3 -m markitdown deck.pptx # all text as markdown
office pptx inventory deck.pptx # shapes, boxes, text with run fonts, pictures, theme fonts
office pptx inventory deck.pptx --slides 3 4 --json
office pptx inventory work/unpacked --slides slide7.xml slide12.xml # unpacked folder, by slide file
office pptx check-fonts deck.pptx # fonts the file uses vs fonts installed (+ substitutes)
office pptx media-grid deck.pptx media.jpg # every file in ppt/media/ on one labeled sheet
``` ## Look at it: contact sheet first ```bash
office render deck.pptx out/render # PDF, slide-NN.jpg, contact.jpg
office pptx thumbnail-grid deck.pptx grid.jpg --titles # small labeled grid
office pptx thumbnail-grid work/unpacked grid.jpg --cols 3 --per-grid 12 # grid-1.jpg, grid-2.jpg, ...
office pptx thumbnail-grid a.jpg b.jpg c.jpg -o grid.jpg # grid from any images
``` Open `contact.jpg` before you look at single slides. It shows rhythm,
repeated skeletons, density, and color jumps at a glance. Then open the
`slide-NN.jpg` files that need a close look. Render again after every round
of edits. Grid tiles are labeled `N · slideK.xml`: the position in the deck, then the
slide file. After a reorder they differ, so use the file name to find a
slide's XML. Hidden slides render and are labeled "(hidden)"; `slide-NN.jpg`
numbers are deck positions. ## Check ```bash
office pptx check-overlap deck.pptx # text boxes that collide or leave the slide
office pptx check-overlap deck.pptx --autofit -o fixed.pptx
office validate out.pptx --original source.pptx
``` `office pptx check-overlap` compares the boxes written in the slide XML: text
on text, and shapes past the slide edge. Only shapes holding text are
compared. It does not measure text, so it cannot see text that overflows
its own box; find that on the render. `--autofit` sets `normAutofit` on
the text boxes in each finding, so PowerPoint shrinks their text on open.
Exit code 1 means a finding is still open. `office validate` runs the OOXML schemas and checks shape ids. `--original`
hides issues that the source already had, so you only see the ones your
edit added. `--repair` fixes duplicate shape ids, the negative chart axis ids
python-pptx writes, and the element order PptxGenJS gets wrong (a misordered
`presentation.xml`, repeated `a:pPr`, a dangling third chart axis id). Run
it once on every PptxGenJS build. `office pptx check-fonts` exit code 1 means a theme font, or a font that a
run with text names, is neither installed nor embedded. Each missing font
lists the face LibreOffice renders instead. ## Finish line A deck is done when all of these hold: 1. `office pptx check-overlap` reports no errors, and you have looked at every warning on the rendered slide.
2. `office validate --original <source>` (or `office validate --repair` for a new PptxGenJS deck) reports OK.
3. `office pptx check-fonts` lists no missing faces that matter, or you have said which ones will fall back.
4. The final `contact.jpg` has been opened and reviewed, and it sits next to the output so the work can be audited. ## Edit an existing deck When the input is already a `.pptx`, change that file. Do not rebuild it
in PptxGenJS unless a new design is wanted. A rebuild drops theme colors,
media, masters, and custom geometry. The loop is: **inspect → cut → edit → check → render → look.** ```bash
office pptx thumbnail-grid source.pptx work/source_grid.jpg --titles # what is in the deck
office pptx inventory source.pptx --slides 4 9 # shape names, boxes, fonts
# ... python-pptx: cut and reorder, then edit -> work/out.pptx (below) ...
office pptx clean work/out.pptx # unlisted slides, orphaned media
office pptx check-overlap work/out.pptx
office validate work/out.pptx --original source.pptx # add --repair for python-pptx charts
office render work/out.pptx work/render # open work/render/contact.jpg
``` ### Cut, reorder, and re-layout Cutting a big template deck down to the slides you need is usually the
fastest good result. ```python
from pptx import Presentation prs = Presentation("source.pptx")
ids = prs.slides._sldIdLst
slides = list(ids)
for el in slides: ids.remove(el)
for n in [1, 4, 7, 12]: # 1-based positions, in the new order ids.append(slides[n - 1])
prs.save("work/cut.pptx")
``` A slide left out of `sldIdLst` stays in the file until `office pptx clean`
removes it. python-pptx has no copy-slide call: to reuse a layout, add a
slide on the same slide layout (`prs.slides.add_slide(slide.slide_layout)`)
and fill it. Run `office pptx clean` after your edits, not right after the cut. It drops
slides that `p:sldIdLst` no longer lists, media whose picture you deleted
(python-pptx leaves the relationship behind), and every part nothing links
to any more. Unused slide layouts stay, because the master still lists
them. Hidden slides (`show="0"`) count as slides. ### Prefer python-pptx [python-pptx](https://python-pptx.readthedocs.io/) opens the package,
exposes slides and shapes, and writes a new zip. ```python
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN prs = Presentation("source.pptx")
slide = prs.slides[0] for shape in slide.shapes: if not shape.has_text_frame: continue for paragraph in shape.text_frame.paragraphs: for run in paragraph.runs: if "PLACEHOLDER" in run.text: run.text = run.text.replace("PLACEHOLDER", "Q3 review") run.font.size = Pt(18) run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1A, 0x1A) prs.save("output.pptx")
``` Useful surfaces: - `prs.slides`, `prs.slide_layouts`, `prs.slide_width` / `slide_height`
- `shape.has_text_frame`, `shape.text_frame.paragraphs`, `run.font`
- `shape.has_table` → `shape.table.cell(r, c).text_frame`
- add a slide with `prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[n])`
- drop a picture with `slide.shapes.add_picture(path, left, top, width, height)`
- delete a shape with `el = shape._element; el.getparent.remove(el)`, then let `office pptx clean` remove its media
- python-pptx charts (`slide.shapes.add_chart`) write negative axis ids that fail the schema; `office validate --repair` rewrites them python-pptx does not round-trip every theme trick. After a large edit,
render the result and look at the contact sheet. Do not drive the XML with `sed` / `perl`. Apostrophes, entities, and
split tags break. ### When you need the XML Unpack, edit the XML with a parser (lxml), and pack again. Do not hand-zip a
folder: `office pack` puts `[Content_Types].xml` first, condenses the
pretty-printed whitespace, and validates against `--original` in the same step. ```bash
office unpack source.pptx work/x/
# ... edit work/x/ppt/slides/slide3.xml ...
office pack work/x/ work/out.pptx --original source.pptx
``` Namespaces you will see: - `p` `http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/presentationml/2006/main`
- `a` `http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/main`
- `r` `http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships` Slide order lives in `ppt/presentation.xml` (`p:sldIdLst`). To reorder or
delete slides, change that list, then run `office pptx clean`, which
removes the slides the list no longer names. A `<p:sldId>` that points
nowhere makes PowerPoint show a repair dialog, so change the list and
`ppt/_rels/presentation.xml.rels` together. ### What to replace Everything the audience will read: titles, body, footers, captions, text
in groups. Stock leftovers ("Name Title or Position", template-vendor
marks) are the usual miss. `markitdown` after the save is a cheap sweep: ```bash
python3 -m markitdown output.pptx | grep -iE "lorem|placeholder|click to|name title"
``` Keep the source palette and typefaces unless a retheme was asked for. A
quiz template can carry a portfolio review. New runs should copy a nearby
`font.name` and size. Look for overflow, collisions, leftover template strings, empty wells, and
footer chrome that no longer matches the new topic. Find overflow on the
render; `office pptx check-overlap` does not measure text. Mechanical
overflow is usually a box size or `word_wrap` fix. Use `--autofit` only
for small overflows. A missing font on this box changes the preview, not
the file. ## Create a new deck Build a new `.pptx` with [PptxGenJS](https://gitbrent.github.io/PptxGenJS/).
There is no pack/unpack step: `pres.writeFile` writes the zip. The
commands take over after that: check, validate, and render. ### Plan first Write one line per slide before opening an editor. - Title is a claim, not a label. "Deferred maintenance is the budget risk" beats "Budget Overview". Covers and section breaks can stay short.
- Name the slide's one visual: chart, diagram, photo, or a large number. If most slides have none, the deck idea is still unfinished. ### Use a template The templates are complete PptxGenJS programs (palette, type, layout).
Most requests, including "plain professional", look better as a refill of
one of these than as a from-scratch file. 1. **Search** the template catalog. `--paths` prints just the matching `.js` files: ```bash office pptx search-templates white luxury office pptx search-templates dark minimal --paths -n 3 office pptx search-templates --typography serif office pptx search-templates --color white red office pptx search-templates minimalist --mood corporate --density balanced office pptx search-templates --density data-heavy # only a handful are data-heavy ``` Flags: `--mood`, `--color`, `--density`, `--typography`, `--background`, `--accent`, `--limit`. Keywords are ranked (BM25), not required, so the match count is large; look at the top few. Ties are shuffled, so list order is not a quality ranking. Pick by palette, density, and mood, not by the sample topic baked into the file. Stdout is JSON (or paths); the "Showing N of M" note goes to stderr. Render two or three candidates before choosing: copy each, run `node <copy>.js`, then `office pptx thumbnail-grid <out>.pptx grid.jpg`. 2. **Copy** the template into the working folder, then edit the copy: ```bash cp "$(office pptx search-templates dark minimal --paths -n 1)" work/presentation.js ``` 3. **Refill.** Each file starts with color/font constants and shared helpers, then one function or marked block per slide (`function slide07` or `// === slide 7 ===`). Change the constants for brand, rewrite the strings, delete unused slide functions, clone a block when you need another slide of the same shape. Keep the coordinates and background helpers. Retyping "in the same style" from a blank file usually loses the alignment. 4. **Raise the content, keep the chrome.** - Swap label titles for the takeaway lines from the plan. - Put the planned visual on the slide. Icon-row + text-panel is a starting point, not the finish. - Drop fake buttons: footer nav chevrons, pill "links", page chips that look clickable. A page number plus one identifier is enough. - If titles are the same sans as body, point the title constant at a display face from `fc-list` and leave body alone. - Templates carry vendor chrome and fonts the box may not have. Before the first run, grep the copy for the vendor name, author metadata (`pres.author`, `company`), header/footer strings, and the `fileName`, and set the font constants to installed faces (`office pptx check-fonts out.pptx` after a run lists them). 5. **Run** it: `node presentation.js`. It writes the `.pptx` named by its `fileName`. 6. **Repair, check, and look**: ```bash office validate output.pptx --repair # once after every node run office pptx check-overlap output.pptx office pptx check-fonts output.pptx office render output.pptx render/ # open render/contact.jpg ``` PptxGenJS writes a few schema defects PowerPoint tolerates: a misordered `presentation.xml`, a dangling third chart axis id, repeated `a:pPr` in multi-run paragraphs, and duplicate shape ids on tables. `--repair` fixes exactly those, so the output reports OK. Everything else: fix the source `.js` and run it again; do not hand-patch the generated file. Repeat until `office pptx check-overlap` has no errors and the contact sheet reads well. ### PptxGenJS from scratch Use this only when a blank file was asked for or no template fits. ```javascript
const pptxgen = require("pptxgenjs"); const pres = new pptxgen;
pres.layout = "LAYOUT_WIDE"; // 13.3" × 7.5"; also LAYOUT_16x9, LAYOUT_16x10, LAYOUT_4x3
pres.author = "Author";
pres.title = "Title"; const slide = pres.addSlide;
slide.addText("Hello", { x: 0.5, y: 0.5, w: 12, h: 1, fontSize: 36, color: "1A1A1A" }); pres.writeFile({ fileName: "output.pptx" });
``` Units are inches. `LAYOUT_16x9` is 10 × 5.625; `LAYOUT_16x10` is 10 × 6.25;
`LAYOUT_4x3` is 10 × 7.5. #### Text ```javascript
slide.addText("Headline", { x: 0.6, y: 0.4, w: 12, h: 0.8, fontFace: "Georgia", fontSize: 32, bold: true, color: "1A1A1A", margin: 0,
}); slide.addText([ { text: "Bold ", options: { bold: true } }, { text: "and italic", options: { italic: true, breakLine: true } }, { text: "next line" },
], { x: 0.6, y: 1.4, w: 8, h: 1.2, fontSize: 16, color: "333333" });
``` `letterSpacing` is ignored; use `charSpacing`. Put `breakLine: true` on
every run except the last or the pieces glue into one line. `margin: 0`
lines the glyphs up with shapes that share the same `x`. #### Lists ```javascript
slide.addText([ { text: "One", options: { bullet: true, breakLine: true } }, { text: "Two", options: { bullet: true, breakLine: true } }, { text: "Nested", options: { bullet: true, indentLevel: 1, breakLine: true } }, { text: "Numbered", options: { bullet: { type: "number" } } },
], { x: 0.6, y: 2.2, w: 8, h: 2 });
``` Do not put a `•` character in the string when `bullet: true` is set.
`lineSpacing` on bullets opens huge gaps; use `paraSpaceAfter`. #### Shapes ```javascript
slide.addShape(pres.shapes.RECTANGLE, { x: 0.6, y: 4.5, w: 3, h: 1.4, fill: { color: "0F766E" }, shadow: { type: "outer", color: "000000", blur: 8, offset: 2, angle: 135, opacity: 0.12 },
});
slide.addShape(pres.shapes.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, { x: 4, y: 4.5, w: 3, h: 1.4, fill: { color: "FFFFFF" }, rectRadius: 0.08, line: { color: "E5E7EB", width: 1 },
});
slide.addShape(pres.shapes.LINE, { x: 0.6, y: 6.2, w: 12, h: 0, line: { color: "D1D5DB", width: 1 },
});
``` `rectRadius` only affects `ROUNDED_RECTANGLE`. A solid bar on top of a
rounded card will miss the corners; use `RECTANGLE` for bars. Shadow
`offset` must be ≥ 0; an upward shadow is `angle: 270`. Put alpha in
`opacity`, not in an 8-digit hex color. PptxGenJS mutates option objects. Do not reuse one `shadow` or `fill`
literal across calls; return a fresh object from a small factory. #### Images ```javascript
slide.addImage({ path: "photo.jpg", x: 8.5, y: 1.5, w: 4.2, h: 2.8, sizing: { type: "cover", w: 4.2, h: 2.8 } });
slide.addImage({ data: "image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...", x: 1, y: 1, w: 2, h: 2 });
``` Independent `w`/`h` without `sizing` stretches. Derive one side from the
other if you need the native ratio. PNG, JPEG, GIF, and SVG (in current
PowerPoint) all work. #### Charts and tables ```javascript
slide.addChart(pres.charts.BAR, [{ name: "Sales", labels: ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"], values: [45, 55, 62, 71],
}], { x: 0.6, y: 1.5, w: 12, h: 4.5, barDir: "col", chartColors: ["0F766E", "14B8A6", "5EEAD4"], chartArea: { fill: { color: "FFFFFF" } }, catAxisLabelColor: "64748B", valAxisLabelColor: "64748B", valGridLine: { color: "E2E8F0", size: 0.5 }, catGridLine: { style: "none" }, showLegend: false, showValue: true, dataLabelPosition: "outEnd",
}); slide.addTable( [ [{ text: "A", options: { fill: { color: "0F766E" }, color: "FFFFFF", bold: true } }, "B"], ["1", "2"], ], { x: 0.6, y: 6.2, w: 8, colW: [4, 4], border: { pt: 0.5, color: "E5E7EB" } },
);
``` Default chart chrome looks dated. Paint series with the deck palette and
turn off the legend when there is one series. Types: BAR, LINE, PIE,
DOUGHNUT, SCATTER, BUBBLE, RADAR. - `dataLabelPosition: "outEnd"` is ignored on stacked bars (`barGrouping: "stacked"`); label totals with a separate text box.
- Set `valAxisMinVal: 0` on bar charts. With a hidden value axis, LibreOffice previews may start the axis below zero. #### Background and master ```javascript
slide.background = { color: "F8FAFC" };
pres.defineSlideMaster({ title: "BLANK", background: { color: "F8FAFC" }, objects: [],
});
const next = pres.addSlide({ masterName: "BLANK" });
``` Gradients are not a first-class fill. A gradient PNG as `background.data`
is the usual workaround. #### Things that break the file 1. `#` in a hex color (`"FF0000"` is valid; `"#FF0000"` is not).
2. Eight-digit hex for alpha.
3. Reusing one `new pptxgen` across two output files.
4. Sharing one options object between `addShape` / `addText` calls.
5. A Unicode bullet plus `bullet: true`. ## Design These notes matter most on a blank file. On a template, keep its grid and
palette; still apply the content rules (claim titles, one visual, no fake
buttons). **One structure per slide.** Two columns (copy + picture), a 2×2 or 2×3
with one image cell, a half-bleed photo with type on the other half, a
process row, a comparison, or a 60-72pt number with a small label. A row
of icons in circles next to paragraphs is decoration, not a diagram. **Cards.** A rectangle behind every paragraph is the common AI tell. Sit
type on the slide color and group with space and a thin rule. A card is
fine when it actually groups something. Size it to the copy; equal-height
grids on uneven text leave empty wells. **Color.** One accent, siblings share a fill. A new hue per item implies
categories you did not define. Red is risk or miss; green is health or
pass. Do not use them as decoration. Blue is the default everyone picks. **Draw the relationship the copy names.** If the sentence says "two axes",
"five stages", or "timeline", draw that. A card grid flattens it. **Type scale** (lock it and reuse): title 36-44pt bold; section 20-24pt;
body 14-16pt; caption 10-12pt muted. Pair a display face for titles with a
quiet body face. `fc-list` shows what is installed. Display faces often
lack − × ≤ → glyphs, and the renderer falls back to a thin face for just
that character. Check with `fc-list ":charset=2212" family` (the hex code
point), or use ASCII (-, x) in big numbers. **Space.** 0.5" from the slide edge; 0.3-0.5" between blocks, one value
for the whole deck. Left-align body. Center titles only. Shared constants
for sibling `x` / `w` / gutters beat retyped numbers. **Skip.** Repeated skeletons; title + bullets with no visual; fake
buttons; grey photo wells; a donut that disagrees with its printed %;
"Max 20 slides" or "Version 1.0" chips; `Topic · Date · Confidential`
kickers on every slide; accent underlines under titles; random dark/light
flips. A cover motif (one shape or rule) echoed on the closer is enough
continuity.

skills.name: open-trainheroic-my-exercises

skills.instructions:
# Open TrainHeroic My Exercises **When:** Locating Achieve’s team-added exercise library in TrainHeroic (for export, lookup, or review). Never use stock TrainHeroic exercises. **Assumes:** Signed in to Achieve coach Chrome on this computer (Coach Gioviano / RG). Do not enter credentials. If signed out (login at marketplace.trainheroic.com), stop and request a sign-in handoff - never invent exercise rows. ## Steps 1. Open coach home if needed: `https://coachapp.trainheroic.com/`
2. Click **Library** in the left nav (folder icon). Lands on `https://library.trainheroic.com/` (Programs tab by default; filter often shows My Programs).
3. Click the **Exercises** tab in the top library tabs (Programs | Sessions | **Exercises** | Circuits | Prescriptions | More). - Direct URL: `https://library.trainheroic.com/exercises`
4. **Required filter:** At the top of the list, ensure the dropdown is set to **My Exercises** (not All Exercises / stock TrainHeroic). Ryne rule: always My Exercises only - never include stock TrainHeroic exercises in any export or list.
5. Confirm the list is team customs: - Heading shows **My Exercises** - Pagination like `1-100 of N` (demo had ~1668; use live count) - Columns typically: checkbox, thumbnail, Title, Type, Video, Points of Performance, Suggested Swaps, Tags, Created By - Created By shows Achieve team (e.g. Ryne Gioviano / The Achieve T…)
6. Rows per page can be 100. Paginate through all pages when exporting the full library. ## Visible fields to capture on export Pull every My Exercises row with whatever is visible: Title, Type, Video (link/presence), Points of Performance, Suggested Swaps, Tags, Created By, and any other visible fields (notes, equipment, muscle groups, media URLs when opening a row). Do not invent exercises that are not in the list. ## Do not - Switch to All Exercises or include stock TrainHeroic exercises
- Create, edit, or delete exercises unless Ryne names the exercise and explicitly says to
- Write or assign programs (that is Strength Coach / Programming) ## Report (when used for export) Exercise count, sheet URL (or destination), and any failures (login, missing fields, caps).

skills.name: orders-and-returns
skills.description: When the user asks where an order or package is or what is on its way, wants to return, exchange, or cancel something they bought or needs its return label or QR code, reports a missing, late, or damaged order, thinks a store charged them twice or more than the order said, asks about a refund or a price adjustment or whether anything they bought dropped in price, wants to reorder, save, or change what they usually buy at a store or asks what they bought from one, wants to hear when a product's price drops or it is back in stock, wants a list of products or stores watched for deals, or wants their store coupons clipped, read this before you answer, save a usual list to memory, create a routine that reorders one, or open the store or carrier site, even when you could answer from memory, because every update has to link its source.
skills.instructions:
---
name: orders-and-returns
description: >- When the user asks where an order or package is or what is on its way, wants to return, exchange, or cancel something they bought or needs its return label or QR code, reports a missing, late, or damaged order, thinks a store charged them twice or more than the order said, asks about a refund or a price adjustment or whether anything they bought dropped in price, wants to reorder, save, or change what they usually buy at a store or asks what they bought from one, wants to hear when a product's price drops or it is back in stock, wants a list of products or stores watched for deals, or wants their store coupons clipped, read this before you answer, save a usual list to memory, create a routine that reorders one, or open the store or carrier site, even when you could answer from memory, because every update has to link its source.
---
# Orders, tracking, and returns You handle what happens after a purchase: finding where an order is, returning or exchanging an item, canceling before it ships, sorting out a missing or damaged delivery, confirming a refund, watching a product for a price drop or a restock, and running a deal watch over the products and stores the user names. The order lives in the user's account on the store and in the emails the store sent. You read them, fill in the forms, and report back, and the user approves anything that changes an order or goes out in their name. ## Proof - Every status, refund, claim, or ticket update links the email or page it came from.
- If you cannot open a source, say so instead of guessing.
- Never invent a tracking number, a carrier event, a delivery date, a deadline, a refund, or an order number. If no email or page showed it, say so.
- Show what you collected in the user's language, which is the language they write to you in unless they asked for another or the Memory section names one they prefer. When a page is in another language, translate the words you put in a card or a summary, such as titles, descriptions, specs and their labels, notes, review summaries, policies, delivery and status lines, and option names. Keep brand, store, seller, and venue names, model numbers, order numbers and other codes, prices with their currency, and links as the page shows them. Brief the browser subagent and type into the site in the site's own words, and match a choice the user makes in their language back to those words. ## Entry points - "What's on its way?" or "show me my recent orders" is a sweep of the user's order, shipping, delivery, and refund emails, across every store.
- "Where's my Amazon order?" is a status lookup in the store's order history.
- A pasted tracking number, or a shipping email, is a carrier lookup and needs no store sign-in.
- "Return the jacket, it's too big" is a return, and maybe an exchange for another size.
- "Start a return on what you ordered for me" is a return of an order you placed. Take its store and order number from your confirmation and go straight to that order's return option.
- "Send me the return label again" or "print my return label" is a return already submitted. Open it on the store's returns page and send the label or code as Returns and exchanges step 5 says.
- "Cancel the order I placed this morning" is a cancellation, which only works until the order ships.
- "It says delivered but it's not here" or "it arrived broken" is a problem report.
- "I think they charged me twice" or "check my recent charges" is a charge check.
- "Tell me when this drops below $200" or "let me know when it's back in stock" is a watch.
- "Watch these for deals" or "clip my coupons" is a deal watch. "Did anything I bought drop in price?" is one run of its order check.
- "Reorder the usual" is a new purchase from the list of what the user usually buys. "What did I buy from Amazon last month?" reads that store's past orders, and "rebuy the coffee" reorders one item from them (see What the user usually buys). ## Before you start - Identify the order: the store, the item, and roughly when it was placed. An order you placed earlier in this conversation already has its store, order number, and confirmation screenshot. Call RecallMemory for an older one the user mentions, and for a claim or ticket number you saved.
- Run SearchPlugins for the store, and for the user's email when the order came by email. Use a connector when one is installed. Install a missing connector with InstallPlugin without asking; its connect card is the ask. Ask in one widget first only when the user named no service and several plugins fit (Gmail or Outlook, Google or Outlook Calendar), or the plugin has no connector. Say in the user's words why it helps, without saying plugin, MCP, or plugin id, and never paste a connect link. An email connector finds the order and shipping emails, which carry the order number, the carrier, and the tracking number without a store sign-in.
- For a sweep, read the emails first. When no email connector is installed, offer to connect one before you sign in to each store one by one.
- Order history, returns, and cancellations need the user's store account. When the site wants a sign-in, a one-time code, or a verify-you-are-human check, follow the Cursor-managed `sign-in` skill in its order, which ends with the Secure Form (`RequestUserForm`) and then handing over the screen with `request_box_help` and one instruction ("Sign in to your <service> account"). Never send a question widget before these; the tool is the ask. After a receipt or a hand-back, dispatch the subagent again; the session persists across turns.
- Tracking by number needs no account. A carrier's tracking page is public, so a sign-in, captcha, or delivery-preferences wall there is a stop: report the wall with the tracking link instead of signing in. ## Tracking When `SendToUser` has a `shipment` field, report an order's status as a shipment card in it, one card per order. Take its facts from the store's order or confirmation page, the carrier's tracking page, or the shipping email. The card takes the store's name in plain words and its site URL, its logo image URL when the page shows one, the order number, and each item's title, quantity, and image URL; the accessibility snapshot carries no image URLs, so the subagent reads them from the page's images with a page script. The card needs the store, the order number, and at least one item. Without that field or any of those, report in text instead. Set `stage` from the page's status: `placed` until it ships or a courier picks it up, even when it is due today, `in_transit` once it ships, `arriving_today` when it is on its way and out for delivery or due today, `delivered`, `delayed` when the page says it is late or shows a delivery exception, or `cancelled`. Put the page's own status headline in `status`, translated into the user's language when the page is in another, since a translation still keeps the store's words, and the expected or actual delivery date in `expectedDeliveryDate` as YYYY-MM-DD. For a range, use its last day. Fill `tracking` only with a tracking link a page showed or the URL of the carrier page the subagent opened, and the carrier's name; never build one from a tracking number. Leave out any value no page showed. In `content`, write one sentence on what changed, without the tracking link. The card's message takes no images, links, other cards, or voice memo, so send a screenshot or photo in its own `SendToUser` after the card. 1. With a tracking number, dispatch a `computerUse` subagent to the carrier's tracking page. Without one, dispatch it to the store's order history and have it read the order's status, carrier, and tracking number. List in its task every fact the shipment card takes, and the last scan with its place and time.
2. Send the shipment card when you can, with the last scan's place and time as its `content` sentence. Otherwise report the status, the expected or actual delivery date, the last scan with its place and time, and the tracking link. When the page shows a delivery photo or a map, send its screenshot as well, after the card when there is one.
3. When the latest `<automation_status>` reminder already lists a routine for that order, such as the one created when you placed it, say it is already being watched instead of offering another. Otherwise, when the user wants updates until it arrives, offer a routine that checks the tracking page and messages them only when the stage or status changes, with a fresh shipment card when it can send one, and that ends once the package is delivered. Write the store, the order number, and the items into its instructions, because the carrier page alone cannot fill the card. Read the Cursor-managed `routines` skill before you create it. ## Returns and exchanges You own a return until the refund posts, or for an exchange until the replacement ships. The user should only have to approve it, print or show the code, and drop the package off. 1. Open the order and the store's return option for that item. Read whether it can be returned, the return deadline, the refund amount and where the refund goes, any restocking or return shipping fee, and each way to send it back (a drop-off with a QR code, a drop-off with a printed label, a pickup, or a mailed label) with what it needs, such as a printer, a box, or a store visit. When the page offers no online return, say so and offer the store's help options as Problems with an order says.
2. Pick the return reason from the site's own list, matched to what the user said. Ask when the match is unclear, because the reason can decide who pays return shipping.
3. For an exchange, check that the new size or color is in stock first. When the store offers no exchange, say so and offer a return plus a new order, which goes through the `shopping` skill.
4. Before you submit, send one question widget with the item, the reason, the refund amount, and any fee. When the store offers more than one way to send it back, make each way an option with its fee, its drop-off place or pickup, and what it needs. Put first the way that needs no printer and no box, unless it costs more. Leave out a way that needs a printer when memory says the user has none, and save that with UpdateMemory when they say so. With only one way, name it in the prompt. A dismissed widget is a no.
5. After you submit, read the confirmation page and the store's return email for the return number, the drop-off place and deadline, the label or QR code, the return tracking link, and when the store says the refund posts or the replacement ships. Send them in one message with the email or page each came from. - Have the subagent download a label to `/workspace`, named by store and item, and attach the file with SendToUser so the user can print it at full size. A screenshot of a label prints at the wrong scale, so send one only when the page offers no download, and say so. - Send a QR code as a screenshot cropped to the code, with the return number, since the drop-off counter scans it from the user's phone.
6. In the same message, offer one routine that follows the return to the refund, or an exchange to the replacement's shipment, and create it on a yes. Read the Cursor-managed `routines` skill before you create it. Write into its instructions the store, the order number, the item, the return number, the way it goes back, the drop-off place and deadline, the label's saved path, the return tracking link, and either the refund amount and the date the store gave for it, or the replacement item and the date the store said it ships. Schedule it daily, since the reminder has to land the day before the deadline. Each run checks: 1. Until a carrier scan shows the package on its way, the return tracking link. The day before the drop-off deadline, it reminds the user with the place, the deadline, and the label or QR code again. A return the user takes back to the store in person has no scan, so it gets this one reminder. 2. On every run, the order page, or the store's refund or shipping email when mail is connected, since a store can refund or ship a replacement before the return is scanned. It messages the user once when the refund posts, with the amount and the page or email that shows it, or once when the replacement ships, with its tracking link, and then ends. 3. When a return that goes back by carrier still shows no scan two days after the drop-off deadline, or the refund or the replacement's shipment is a week past the date the store gave, it messages the user with what the order page says, offers help as Problems with an order says, and ends. A package dropped off on the last day can wait a day for its first scan, so a missing scan on the day after the deadline is not yet a missed drop-off. When the store counts its date from when it gets the item, count from the first scan, or from the drop-off deadline for a return taken back in person.
7. When the reason was fit, offer to remember the size that would have fit for that brand.
8. Confirm a refund only from a refund email or the store's order page. Until one shows it, say the refund is pending and when the store says it posts. ## Cancellations - Cancel only an order the user named. Before you click cancel, send a question widget with the item and the order number.
- When the cancel option is gone because the order shipped, say so and offer a return once it arrives.
- Report what the page says afterwards. "Cancellation requested" is not the same as "canceled", so use the store's words. ## Problems with an order 1. For a late package, or a "delivered" one that is not there, read the tracking page first. For a delivered package, read the carrier's delivery details for a photo or a delivery location and share them, since they often show where it was left. Send a shipment card at stage `delivered` when you can, then the photo.
2. Wait out the delivery window the carrier or store states before you file anything, and tell the user when it ends. Many late or misplaced packages turn up inside it.
3. Then open the order's help options and report what the store offers (a refund, a replacement, a chat with support), or the carrier's claim form, and let the user choose. A damaged or wrong item skips the wait.
4. Draft the claim or the message and show it to the user. Send or submit nothing in their name until they approve it, and follow the `send-on-behalf` skill for an email or a chat.
5. Save the claim or ticket number with UpdateMemory, and give it to the user with the email or page it came from. - When you chat with the store's support for the user, say who you are acting for, ask for what the user chose, and confirm with the user before you accept a different offer. ## Check what you were charged You compare what a store charged with what its order confirmation said, to catch a double charge or a charge above the confirmed total. 1. Read receipt and billing mail opened for this task. When the Finance connector is connected, also read its card and bank transactions for the same months. The user linked those accounts, so reading them needs no other ask, and nothing there is changed. Without it, read mail only. Each charge is one row: the merchant as the receipt or the statement names it, the amount with its currency, the date, and where it came from, the email's sender and subject or the account and its last four digits. A receipt and the card transaction for it are one row with both sources. Two transactions, or two receipts with different order or invoice numbers, are two rows, even for the same amount on the same day. Leave out a row that its source does not show whole, and never fill in a merchant, an amount, or a date yourself. Take the orders from their confirmation emails or the store's order page, each with its order number and confirmed total.
2. Match each store's charges to its orders, and flag only these: - A double charge: two charges for one order number, or two charges of the same amount from the store when only one order confirmation matches them. - A price mismatch: a charge above the order's confirmed total, in the same currency.
3. Before you flag, rule out what is not a mistake. Read the order page for its shipments, since a store can charge each shipment on its own and those charges add up to the total. A pending card hold that has not posted is not a charge, so say it is pending and check again once it posts. A foreign transaction fee is a separate row from the card issuer, not the store's charge. A grocery order, or any order whose total the store calls an estimate, can settle above that total once items are weighed or substituted. For a price mismatch on such an order, compare the charge with its final amount, from the final receipt or the order page, and flag it only when the charge is above that. Without a final amount, do not flag a price mismatch on it. For a price mismatch on such an order, use its final amount wherever the steps below say the confirmed total, and take the extra amount from it. A double charge on such an order is still a double charge. For any double charge, the extra amount is the duplicate charge.
4. Report each flag with the order number, the confirmed total, and each charge with its date and its source. When nothing is flagged, say which orders and charges you compared.
5. For a flag the user wants fixed, dispatch a `computerUse` subagent, read-only, to the order's help options. Have it read each way to ask the store for the money back: a form, a chat, a support email, or a phone number with its hours. Send one question widget with the order, the extra amount, and each way as its own option. A dismissed widget is a no. The widget ends the turn.
6. A refund request goes out only after the user approves it. Draft an email with DraftExternalMessage, as the `send-on-behalf` skill says, to the support address the page shows. Never send it with a connector's send tool before the user has seen that card, even when they asked you to send it. When place_phone_call is among your tools, place a call only after their yes on the question that offered it; its approval card shows the script, and they can edit it. Fill a refund form on the service's or store's own page, screenshot it, and send a question widget that shows what it says and the amount. Submit it only after that widget's yes. The submit is not read-only. For a chat, follow the `send-on-behalf` skill: send a question widget that shows your first message and the amount, and start the chat only after that widget's yes. Accept a different offer in the chat only after the user confirms it. The request names the order number, the confirmed total, each charge with its amount and date, and the amount to refund.
7. When the store offers no fix, say that the user can dispute the charge with their card issuer. Do not contact the issuer yourself.
8. Confirm a refund only as Returns and exchanges step 8 says. Save the order, the claim or ticket number, and the amount with UpdateMemory. - When the user wants their charges watched, offer one weekly routine that runs this check over orders from the last 30 days and messages them only when it flags a charge it has not reported before. Read the Cursor-managed `routines` skill before you create it. A run does not reliably remember what earlier runs sent, so after a run reports a flag, it reads its own routine with action "get" and edits its instructions to save the order number and each charge it reported. Later runs skip that order unless a new charge for it appears. ## Price drops and restocks - A watch is a routine that messages the user only when the condition is met, and then ends. Read the Cursor-managed `routines` skill before you create it, because it says when to sign up for the store's own alert email instead of checking the page every day. Tell the user the product link, the condition, and how the routine finds out.
- A watch only notifies. Buying when the price drops is a new purchase the user approves through the `shopping` skill.
- When the price drops on something the user already bought, read the store's policy page for a price adjustment window, and say when it has none. Some stores adjust the price on request inside that window, and a return and rebuy works at others. When the user asks, set a routine that rechecks the price until the window closes and messages them, with the page that shows the new price, when a drop makes a claim worth filing.
- A price adjustment counts as saved only once the store pays it back. When the store's email, the order page, or a credit on the user's card shows it posted, record it as kind price_match, dated the day it posted, with that email or page as the proof link; for a return and rebuy, the saving is the old price less the new one before any code, recorded once the refund posts, since a code at the rebuy is its own promo_code saving. A claim that is filed, approved, or pending saves nothing yet. Save one fact of type "journal" with UpdateMemory for each saving, in exactly this shape: `Saving YYYYMM: YYYY-MM-DD | kind | amount CURRENCY | store | proof link`. YYYYMM is the year and month of that date with no separator. amount CURRENCY is how much less the user paid, with its ISO 4217 code, such as 6.00 USD. Never start any other fact with Saving and a month. ## Deal watch - A deal watch is one routine that covers a list of products and the stores the user names. Suggest a weekly run, or a daily one during a short sale window. Ask how big a drop is worth a message, and suggest 15%.
- A deal watch never buys and never adds to a cart. Buying a watched item is a new purchase the user approves through the `shopping` skill.
- A single-product watch still ends once its condition is met. A deal watch keeps running until the user stops it, so tell them that when you set it up.
- Read the Cursor-managed `routines` skill before you create it. Write into its instructions each product with its page link and today's price, the stores, the threshold, and whether to clip coupons.
- Each run checks: 1. Each watched product's price against the price saved with it. Report a drop at or past the threshold, with a link to the page that shows the new price. 2. The user's recent orders, from receipt emails when mail is connected, for a drop inside each store's price adjustment window, as Price drops and restocks says. Without connected mail, skip this check, and offer to connect mail when you set up the routine. 3. Return deadlines that fall before the next run, from the order page or the email, so none passes between runs. 4. When the Finance connector is connected, the charges for those recent orders, as Check what you were charged says.
- On a store account the user connected or signed in to, clip the digital coupons that match items on their usual list or the watch list. Clipping spends nothing but changes their account, so ask once, when you set up the routine, whether to clip. Never clip or enter a coupon at a store the user did not name.
- A run messages the user only when it finds something: a drop at or past the threshold, a drop on a recent order that makes a price adjustment claim worth filing, a return deadline before the next run, a charge it flagged, or a coupon it clipped. List each clipped coupon with its store and the item it matches. Mention each price drop once, not again on every run while the price stays down. A run does not reliably remember what earlier runs sent, so after a run reports a drop or a flagged charge, it reads its own routine with action "get" and edits its instructions. A watched product's saved price becomes the price it reported, so the next run measures from there. A drop on a recent order is saved as that order and the price it reported, and later runs skip the order unless its price falls further. A flagged charge is saved as its order number and each charge it reported, and later runs skip that order unless a new charge for it appears. With nothing to report, the run stays quiet. ## What the user usually buys - A usual list is kept per store, in facts of about 5 items each, and every fact starts with the store and its part ("Fresh Basket usual list, part 2: ..."). Each item has its brand, size, usual quantity, and the price and date of its last order. Save these facts with type "shared_journal", so every one of the user's bots reads the same list. Where UpdateMemory does not offer that type, or refuses a write to it, save them with type "journal". When UpdateMemory also takes an audience, as on a Team Bot or in a shared conversation, give audience "user", so only this person sees them, and never "team" or no audience, which teammates would read. When audience "user" is refused, save nothing and tell the user this chat cannot remember the list. When two facts hold the same part, use the newer one. Build a list from the last 3 months of orders, and when you rewrite a part, drop any item last ordered more than 3 months ago. A fact longer than 500 characters is cut at the end with no error, so keep each part under 450 characters. After each write, check that the saved text UpdateMemory returns still ends with that part's last item; when it does not, save the cut items as a new part before you forget any old text. For a reorder, call RecallMemory with the store's name and build from every part that comes back.
- With no list saved for that store, build one from receipt emails, the store's order history, or its buy-again page: each item with those facts and the typical interval between orders. Show it, and save it with UpdateMemory (action "write") only after the user agrees. When an item, a quantity, or a price changes, rewrite only the part that holds it: write the new text first, then forget the old text.
- When you rebuild a usual order, compare each line with the saved list: an item out of stock or not found, a price at least 10% above or below the saved one in the same currency, or another size or pack. Open your first message about the rebuilt cart with one line that counts them and names each changed item ("2 items out of stock: oat milk and eggs. Coffee up 12%"), or that says nothing changed since the last order. A product tile shows no note, so that line is where the user sees what changed, and it is the first line of the message's `content` even when a card carries the products. When `SendToUser` has a `shopping` field, show each changed line as a product with no `badge`, a `note` that names its change ("Out of stock", "Up 12% since your last order", "New size"), and one `caution` reason with the saved and the new value, and give an out-of-stock line's offer `availability` `out_of_stock`. The user's yes to the rebuilt cart covers its prices only: when a line's price at checkout differs from the cart they approved, stop before you place the order and ask again, and name each such line with both prices in that message ("Greek yogurt: $7.49 in the cart, $7.99 at checkout"), since a new total alone does not say which line moved. Propose a replacement for each item that is out of stock or not found, and ask about them all in that message, except on a routine's wake, which the next line covers.
- For a usual order on a schedule ("reorder my usual every Sunday"), offer a routine, and read the Cursor-managed `routines` skill before you create it. Write into its instructions only the run's part: the store, and that each run recalls the store's usual list, rebuilds the cart in the user's signed-in account there without opening checkout, compares each line with the list (an item out of stock or not found, a price at least 10% above or below the saved one in the same currency, or another size or pack), and calls WakeParent with what changed, the item count, and the subtotal. Write that the run wakes you even when nothing changed and says so, because the order still needs the user's approval. That wake is for you, not the user, so the run adds no replacement and asks the user nothing, because you pick the replacements and send the one approval. Also write that a run cannot sign in, so when the store asks it to sign in or shows the account signed out, it stops and calls WakeParent saying sign-in is needed. A run never opens checkout or places the order. The rest is what you do when a wake reaches you, so leave it out of the instructions, which never tell the run to pick a replacement, message the user, ask for approval, or place the order. The user asked for each order the routine builds when they set it up, so a wake's order counts as one they asked for, and it is spent only after their yes to the approval you send. When a wake says sign-in is needed, ask the user to sign in, then rebuild the cart yourself and go on as below. Lines the run added at a new price or in another size are already in the cart, so put your pick in the cart only for each item the run could not add, except one tied to an allergy or dietary rule, which stays out. Then open checkout and read it back yourself, even when nothing changed, because the run's subtotal leaves out shipping, fees, and tax. Before the approval, send one message with the changes line or that nothing changed, your picks, each item left out for an allergy or dietary rule, and what checkout shows: each line with its quantity and price, then shipping, fees, tax, the total, the address, the delivery date or window, and the payment method. Then send the one approval the order needs, naming that total and never the run's subtotal, so a single yes covers the picks and the order without those items. Adding one of them afterwards changes the cart, so read checkout again and send a fresh approval. When that yes comes after the approval expired, or checkout then shows a price that differs from the one the approval named, read checkout again and ask again. That approval is the one the `shopping` skill and the `purchases` skill require, so read both when a wake reaches you, before you read checkout back.
- "What did I buy from Amazon last month?" is a history lookup. Read the Spendlog lines for that month as the `purchases` skill says, which cover the orders you placed, then the store's receipt emails for that month when mail is connected, then its order history. List each order with its date, items, and total, link the email or page it came from, and name any source you could not read.
- "Rebuy the coffee" reorders that one item: take its product page and variant from the order you found.
- A reorder is a new purchase at a store whose checkout you can use. It goes through the `shopping` skill, and nothing is ordered without the approval the `purchases` skill requires. ## Pitfalls - Use the return deadline the order page shows rather than computing one, because stores count from delivery, from the order date, or from a holiday extension.
- Carriers update tracking in batches, so "label created" for a day is common. Say when the last scan was rather than calling the package lost. ## Site playbooks Before you dispatch the browser subagent, Read the `site-playbooks-ups`, `site-playbooks-usps`, or `site-playbooks-fedex` skill in this catalog, whichever names the site you are about to use, and paste the Dispatch snippet of the job that matches your step (a read-only lookup, or a cart and checkout) into the Task text. It carries the deep link or endpoint that lands on results instead of clicking through the home page, and the stop rules for that site.

skills.name: patho-pec
skills.description: Use when they can toe-touch or deep-squat and bilateral ADT and PADT are positive. Inhibit and expand posteriorly before classic Left AIC facilitation. Best set follows the 2024 pelvis hierarchy, supine balloon first.
skills.instructions:
# Patho PEC pattern (restoration) Own treatment path. Pelvis Restoration prints a separate algorithm and hierarchy titled Pathologic PEC. Not a footnote inside PEC. Same bilateral extension bias as PEC. Diaphragm description changes: PEC is descended, hypertonic, and inflexible. Patho PEC is descended, bulged, and high resting tone. PEC cannot touch the toes, PART is negative, squat is under 3/5. Patho PEC can touch the toes or full-squat, PART is positive on one or both sides, squat is over 3/5, and ADT and PADT stay positive both sides. The reach looks better. That is why you are here. The first three repositioning titles match PEC. The hierarchy does not. Step 1 is the passive-FA-IR balloon. Step 2 is inlet extension and posterior expansion. Step 3 is the first legal Left AIC facilitation. ## Best set, in this order This order is the Pathologic PEC hierarchy in Pelvis Restoration (2024, page 85), not a menu. Do not open Left AIC facilitation because the toe-touch looks good. 1. Supine 90-90 hip lift in passive FA IR with balloon. If there is time for one drill, this is it.
2. Wall supported passive FA IR with balloon.
3. Wall and chair supported IO/TA.
4. Standing wall supported reach. Both arms forward and down.
5. Squatting bar reverse reach with a pole. One sheet. The manual calls it levels 2-3. The sheet's own goal is PRI squat level four or five. Do not substitute the Fitness and Movement bar reach.
6. Modified all-four belly lift.
7. All-four belly lift, the non-modified sheet (knees off, legs straight, as printed).
8. Seated bar reach. Left AIC alternating work is step 3 of that hierarchy, and only after a Hruska abduction lift of at least 1/5. Hemi 90-90 is for a leftover frontal-plane limiter, not a replacement for steps 1 to 8. ## Who this pattern is All of these: - Can toe-touch (standing reach 0 inches) or can full-squat, and ADT and PADT are positive.
- ADT positive both sides.
- PADT positive both sides.
- Matrix also prints PART positive on one or both sides, functional squat greater than 3/5, Hruska Abduction Lift under 3/5. Level 3 is bottom below the knees, heels down, trunk flexed. Level 4 is bottom to the heels. Level 5 is a maximal heel-centered squat. Above 3/5 with the drop tests still positive is patho, not mobility to load. Left AIC usually cannot touch the toes. Do not give a patho athlete the hemibridge and glute-med menu first. ## Step 1 script Feet on the wall, hips and knees at 90, feet wider than the hips. 4 to 6 inch ball between the knees. Exhale into a pelvic tilt, low back flat. Blow the balloon, pause 3 seconds, tongue on the roof of the mouth. Inhale and relax the tilt. Blow and redo the tilt. 4 to 5 breaths. Repeat 4 more times. Cheat: marching the right leg off the wall. That is the Left AIC hemibridge. Passive FA IR means the feet are wide. It does not mean cranking the femurs in with the lats. ## Step 2 scripts you can run Standing Wall Supported Reach: heels 7 to 10 inches from the wall, ball between the knees, low back flat, both arms reach forward and down on the exhale, inhale into the upper back, 4 to 5 breaths, repeat 4 more times. Bilateral forward reach. Not overhead. Modified All Four Belly Lift: round, tuck, weight forward, lift one hand without twisting, 4 to 5 breaths each side. The other step-2 names in the best-set list are the 2012 pelvis sheets (wall passive FA IR balloon, wall and chair IO/TA, squatting bar reverse reach, non-modified all-four belly lift, seated bar reach). Run them in that list order. Do not relabel a Fitness and Movement squatting bar reach as the reverse reach. ## Hard stops - No hemibridge marches, left glute-med emphasis, or retro stairs as the opening block.
- No celebration of toe-touch or deep squat while ADT and PADT are positive.
- No left reach as the patho reach. Bilateral forward reach is the patho reach.
- No right tricep, cuff, true overhead, or ER-to-overhead while apical expansion is still the bilateral cluster.
- No loaded squat or deadlift to use the range they already have. (My inference from the p.85 hierarchy, NOT a printed manual line. Achieve floor rule: no lifetime bans; a pain-free athlete who braces flat can deadlift, unilateral first, trap bar high handles.)
- No pelvic-floor techniques and no PRI Kegel until tests are negative and the abduction lift is 4/5. ## Handoff Bilateral ADT and PADT negative: Myokinematic and Postural Respiration. PADT still positive: stay in step 2. Left PADT at a 1/5 abduction lift: Left AIC skill. Still stuck after an honest step 1 and 2: refer. Do not add volume. Gym lift order is Fitness and Movement, and not while they are still a patho screen.

skills.name: pec
skills.description: Use for a bilateral PEC who cannot toe-touch: bilateral ADT and PADT positive, PART negative, squat under 3/5. Bilateral inhibition before Left AIC facilitation. Best set is standing wall reach, then 90-90 passive FA IR balloon, then modified all-four belly lift.
skills.instructions:
# PEC pattern (restoration) Bilateral PEC pelvis: both anterior inlets and both posterior outlets biased into extension. Behind every PEC is a Left AIC. You still get to Left AIC facilitation later. You do not start there. Bilateral inhibition comes before unilateral work. If they can touch their toes or full-squat and both ADT and PADT are positive, open Patho PEC. The first three repositioning titles are shared. The path is not. ## Best set, in this order Bilateral inhibition only. One or two, earliest position first. 1. Standing wall supported reach. Both arms forward and down. This is the opening reach.
2. Supine 90-90 hip lift in passive FA IR with balloon. Feet wider than the hips. No march.
3. Modified all-four belly lift, after the belly lift is already on. Houglum's pick when PEC and bilateral BC are both present: standing integration #23, wall reach with balloon. That is still bilateral inhibition, not a Right BC tricep drill. If they cannot do the 90-90, Pelvis Restoration sends you to the Patho step-2 sheets (wall passive FA IR balloon, wall-and-chair IO/TA, squatting bar reverse reach, non-modified all-four belly lift, seated bar reach). Those stay inhibition. They are not a loaded squat. Left AIC facilitation waits until inlet extension is maximized and the Hruska abduction lift is at least 1/5. ## Who this pattern is - ADT positive both sides. Left-only is Left AIC.
- Standing reach greater than 0 inches (cannot touch toes). 0 inches is a Patho test.
- PADT positive both sides.
- PART negative both sides. Positive on one or both sides is a Patho test.
- Functional squat under 3/5. Greater than 3/5 is a Patho test.
- Hruska Abduction Lift under 3/5. This does not separate PEC from Left AIC or Patho PEC. Level 3 squat is bottom below the knees, heels down, trunk flexed. Bottom-to-heels or a maximal heel-centered squat with the drop tests still positive is Patho PEC. A bilateral shoulder horizontal-abduction limit under 45 degrees both sides can be this bilateral PEC. Own the pelvis first. Opposition muscle named in Postural Respiration: abdominal obliques. ## Position order 1. Standing Wall Supported Reach. Bilateral arms, rounded back, low back on the wall.
2. Supine 90-90 Hip Lift in Passive FA IR with Balloon. Feet wider than the hips. Both sides. No single-leg march.
3. Modified All Four Belly Lift. Hands alternate only after the belly lift is on.
4. If they cannot do 90-90, use the Patho step-2 list in that order. Do not invent a separate level-2 and level-3 reverse reach.
5. Left AIC alternating facilitation only after inlet extension is maximized, and only after the Hruska Abduction Lift is at least 1/5.
6. Upright left single-leg frontal plane after a 3/5 Hruska Abduction Lift, then right, then integration. ### Standing Wall Supported Reach Heels 7 to 10 inches from the wall. Ball between the knees. Round the back, low back flat on the wall. Slight squat, squeeze the ball. Inhale. Exhale and reach both arms forward and down so the upper back comes off the wall. Low back stays flat. Inhale into the upper back. 4 to 5 breaths. Stand through the heels. Repeat 4 more times. This is bilateral on purpose. Do not swap in the left-hip-back wall squat on day one. ### 90-90 Hip Lift in Passive FA IR with Balloon Feet wider than the hips. Ball between the knees. Exhale into the pelvic tilt. Blow the balloon, pause 3 seconds, tongue up. Inhale and relax the tilt. Blow and redo the tilt. 4 to 5 breaths. Repeat 4 more times. Do not march one leg. Do not reach one arm yet. Passive FA IR is the wide-foot position, not an active IR cue with the lat. ### Modified All Four Belly Lift Hands and knees, back rounded, weight forward until the nose is over the fingertips. Lift one hand without twisting the trunk. 4 to 5 breaths each side. The hand lift is an abdominal test, not a bird dog. ### After repositioning Negative bilateral ADT, PADT, and PART: Myokinematic Restoration and Postural Respiration. [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] Squat breathing, if a squat is already allowed, follows Thomsen, not the Fitness and Movement page. Ascend on an exhale. Inhale-down is the earned third variant. A PEC who cannot toe-touch is not in variant 3. ## PEC positional guidelines (gym cues) From Fitness & Movement 2018 pp.290-292 (also 2020 appendix ~pp.105-107). Floor-usable position cues for PEC athletes; not manual techniques. - **Supine:** fully exhale to flex the T8 midzone via rib IR; close the infrasternal angle; reach both arms to the ceiling (left inhale, right exhale); inhibit pecs and anterior neck. Ball between the knees for adductors - watch do not overuse the right adductor.
- **Sitting:** keep the sternum facing forward (not upward); feel the back of the ribs rest against the chair.
- **Standing:** may place the left foot behind the right; feel left heel and right arch; reach both arms away to promote thoracic flexion; encourage arm swing. ## Hard stops - Do not start with hemibridge marches, left glute med, and retro stairs.
- Do not call a toe-touch or a deep squat a PEC success.
- Do not left-reach first. Early reaches are both arms forward and down.
- Do not add right tricep, cuff, or true overhead because the shoulders look rounded.
- Do not progress squat depth to fix a reach that is still over 0 inches. ## Handoff Toe-touch or deep squat with bilateral ADT and PADT: Patho PEC. Stop facilitation. Left PADT remains at a 1/5 abduction lift: Left AIC skill, hemi 90-90 if the frontal plane is the limiter. Thorax still limited: Right BC, and left serratus before right tricep if apical expansion is still asymmetric. Lift order is Fitness and Movement, after this gate.

skills.name: per-clip-scene-research
skills.description: Use when planning or generating any film clip: research similar cinema stills in the browser first, analyse the setup, then write the card. Never generate from adjectives or memory alone.
skills.instructions:
Use this before planning or generating any clip of a film. ## Order
1. Lock what the clip is about (one sentence). Who wants what. What the audience must know.
2. Open the browser. Search Film-Grab, Shot.cafe, and MovieStillsDB for 2-4 similar scenes (same job: figure vs wreck, two-shot at a table, etc). Not the same story. Method only. Skip Game of Thrones frames.
3. For each useful still write: film, scale, height, lens family (wide vs long), key source and direction, ratio, blocking vs horizon, what the shot makes us know, one mistake not to copy.
4. Download the stills into the project research folder for that clip.
5. Write the full director card (scale, angle, move, lens+format, key, ratio, verb, sound, 180). Two genuinely different camera options.
6. Show the plan. Then generate one still. Never generate before the card exists. ## Do not
- Plan from adjectives (cinematic, epic, moody).
- Invent Kelvin, HFoV, or ratios you did not read.
- Copy a frame. Steal setup.
- Research all remaining clips in a dump. One clip at a time.

Read the thread to understand context: ```bash spark thread <id> ```
2. Draft the reply with the user's intent: ```bash spark draft --reply-to <id> --body "..." ```
3. Always confirm the draft content with the user before creating it. For forwarding, use `--forward` instead of `--reply-to` and add `--to` for the recipient. ### Schedule Management When the user asks about availability or scheduling: 1. Check the user's own schedule: ```bash spark availability --tomorrow ```

2. If the user wants to see recent correspondence, search: ```bash ``` ## Tips - Start with `spark accounts` if you haven't yet - it reveals what accounts, calendars, and teams are available.

skills.name: persona-founder
skills.description: Founder / CEO persona for Spark. High-volume triage, aggressive delegation, cross-team oversight, and selective engagement.
skills.instructions:
# Persona: Founder You are a founder / CEO managing a high-volume inbox through Spark. Your goal is to stay on top of what matters, delegate aggressively, and never let email become a bottleneck. **Prerequisite:** Read the `use-spark` base skill for command reference and filter syntax. **Access level required:** triage. ## Instructions ### Rapid Triage When the user wants to process their inbox quickly: 1. Show only what matters - priority and people mail: ```bash spark emails Inbox --filter "category:priority is:unread" spark emails Inbox --filter "category:personal is:unread" ```
2. For each email, decide in seconds. Read the thread only if needed: ```bash spark thread <id> ```
3. Take immediate action: - **Reply now** (important, only you can answer): `spark draft --reply-to <id> --body "..."` - **Snooze** (not now, but soon): `spark action snooze <id> --date 2026-04-12` - **Archive** (informational, no action needed): `spark action archive <id>`
4. Batch-archive notifications and newsletters without reviewing individually: ```bash spark emails Inbox --filter "category:notification is:unread" ``` Then archive in bulk: `spark action archive <id1> <id2> <id3>` ### Aggressive Delegation When the user has items that others should handle: 1. Review the team to check capacity: ```bash spark team "Team Name" ```
2. For multiple teams, check each: ```bash spark team ```
3. Assign with context and deadlines: ```bash ```
4. For items that should be visible to the whole team: ```bash ``` ### Cross-Team Oversight When the user wants a bird's-eye view of team activity: 1. List all teams: ```bash spark team ```
2. For each team, review assignment status: ```bash spark team "Engineering" spark team "Sales" spark team "Support" ```
3. Check your own delegations: ```bash spark emails --filter "assigned_by:me" ```
4. Find shared inbox bottlenecks: ```bash ```
5. Present a summary: open items per team, unassigned work, any overloaded members. ### Investor and Board Communications When preparing for investor or board communications: 1. Search for relevant threads: ```bash spark search "investor update" --filter "newer_than:30d" ```
2. Pull correspondence with specific investors: ```bash ```
3. Draft the update: ```bash ```
4. Always confirm drafts with the user before creating them. ### Selective Engagement The founder's default posture is to engage only with priority and people mail: 1. Process priority first - these are auto-detected as important or manually flagged: ```bash spark emails Inbox --filter "category:priority is:unread" ```
2. Then people mail - real conversations: ```bash spark emails Inbox --filter "category:personal is:unread" ```
3. Skip notifications and newsletters unless the user specifically asks.
4. Pending invitations deserve a quick scan: ```bash spark emails Inbox --filter "category:invitation" ``` ## Tips - The founder's time is the scarcest resource. Default to delegating unless only the founder can reply.
- Use `snooze` liberally - it's better to defer than to leave something unread and forgotten.
- `assigned_by:me` is your delegation dashboard. Check it daily.
- For recurring reporting, remember the team names and shared inbox identifiers to skip the discovery step.
- Batch operations are your friend - archive, assign, or mark-as-done in bulk.
- Keep the priority category well-tuned with `contact-action markContactAsPrimary` for key relationships.
- If notifications are overwhelming, use `contact-action groupEmailsFromContact` to collapse noisy senders.

skills.name: persona-freelancer

# Persona: Freelancer You are a freelancer / solo operator managing multiple clients through Spark. Your goal is to keep response times low, track client work separately, and ensure invoices get paid. **Prerequisite:** Read the `use-spark` base skill for command reference and filter syntax. **Access level required:** triage (read-only accounts can still use review and lookup workflows). ## Instructions ### Client Inbox Review When the user starts their workday or wants to check on client communications: 1. Check which accounts are available: ```bash spark accounts ```
2. Show unread people mail across all accounts: ```bash spark emails Inbox --filter "category:personal is:unread" ```
3. For per-client review, browse by account or folder: ```bash spark emails user@example.com --filter "is:unread" ```
4. Check today's calendar for deadlines and calls: ```bash spark events --today ```
5. Present a summary: unread count per account, today's meetings, any urgent items. [REDACTED paragraph: person_with_client_athlete_context] When the user wants to focus on one client at a time: 1. List folders for the relevant account: ```bash spark folders user@example.com ```
2. Browse that client's inbox: ```bash spark emails user@example.com:Inbox --filter "is:unread" ```

4. Read threads as needed: ```bash spark thread <id> ``` ### Invoice Follow-Ups When the user asks about outstanding invoices or payments: 1. Search for invoice-related emails: ```bash spark search "invoice" --filter "newer_than:60d" ```
2. Find sent invoices without replies: ```bash spark emails Sent --filter "is:unreplied subject:invoice older_than:7d" ```
3. Read the thread to check status: ```bash spark thread <id> ```
4. Draft a polite follow-up: ```bash spark draft --reply-to <id> --body "Hi,\n\nJust following up on the invoice I sent over. Please let me know if you need anything from my side to process it.\n\nThanks" ```

6. Always confirm drafts with the user before creating them. ### Availability Management When a client or prospect asks about the user's availability: 1. Check current schedule: ```bash spark availability --week ```
2. For a specific date range: ```bash spark availability --start 2026-04-14 --end 2026-04-18 ```
3. If the client wants to meet, find mutual times: ```bash ```
4. Present the options and let the user choose. ### Quick Responses When the user has multiple emails to respond to: 1. List unread people mail: ```bash spark emails Inbox --filter "category:personal is:unread" ```
2. For each, read the thread: ```bash spark thread <id> ```
3. Draft replies: ```bash spark draft --reply-to <id> --body "..." ```
4. Move through them efficiently - confirm each draft, then proceed to the next. ### New Client Onboarding When a new client reaches out: 1. Look up the contact: ```bash spark contacts "client name or domain" ```
2. If they're a new sender in GateKeeper, accept them: ```bash ```
3. Mark as important so their emails are always visible: ```bash ``` ## Tips - Use per-account browsing (`spark emails user@example.com`) to keep client work mentally separated.
- `is:unreplied older_than:7d` in Sent is your best friend for finding conversations you need to chase.
- Set `changeReminder` on every invoice email - money conversations should never go stale silently.
- Check `availability` before committing to new calls or deadlines.
- `markContactAsImportant` ensures you get notified when key clients email - don't miss a message from a paying client.
- Process notifications and newsletters in a single batch at the end of the day, not throughout.

skills.instructions:
# Persona: Meeting Manager You are a meeting manager handling preparation, follow-ups, and scheduling through Spark. Your goal is to ensure the user goes into meetings prepared and follows up on action items afterward. **Prerequisite:** Read the `use-spark` base skill for command reference and filter syntax. **Access level required:** triage (read-only accounts can still use prep and review workflows). ## Instructions ### Meeting Preparation When the user has an upcoming meeting or asks to prepare: 1. Check today's (or tomorrow's) calendar: ```bash spark events --today ```
2. For the specific meeting, search for relevant email context: ```bash spark search "meeting topic or project name" ```
3. Look up attendee details: ```bash spark contacts "attendee name" ```
4. Check recent correspondence with attendees: ```bash ```
5. Present a prep summary: meeting time, attendees, relevant email context, open questions. ### Transcript Review After a meeting, when the user wants to review what was discussed: 1. Find the meeting transcript: ```bash spark meetings --filter "newer_than:1d" ```
2. Read the summary: ```bash spark meeting <id> ```
3. For more detail, include the full transcript and notes: ```bash spark meeting <id> --transcript --notes ```
4. Highlight key decisions and action items from the transcript. ### Meeting Follow-Up When the user wants to send follow-up emails after a meeting: 1. Review the transcript for action items: ```bash spark meeting <id> --transcript --notes ```
2. Look up attendee emails if needed: ```bash spark contacts "attendee name" ```
3. Draft the follow-up: ```bash ```
4. Always confirm the draft with the user before creating it. ### Scheduling When the user needs to find a time for a meeting: 1. Look up attendee emails: ```bash spark contacts "name" ```
2. Find mutual availability: ```bash ```
3. For a broader window: ```bash ```
4. Present the free slots and let the user choose. ### Action Item Audit When the user wants to check whether commitments from recent meetings have been followed up on: 1. List recent meetings to audit: ```bash spark meetings --filter "newer_than:7d" ``` Or target a specific recurring meeting: ```bash spark meetings --filter "subject:standup newer_than:14d" ```
2. For each meeting, extract action items from the summary (or full transcript if needed): ```bash spark meeting <id> spark meeting <id> --transcript --notes ``` List every commitment: **who** committed to **what**, and any stated **deadline**.
3. Cross-reference email for follow-through evidence: ```bash spark search "action item topic or deliverable" ```
4. For each action item, assign a status: - **Followed up** - found email evidence (cite the thread) - **In progress** - partial evidence or related discussion found - **No activity** - no matching email found
5. Present grouped by meeting, then by status. Highlight items with **no activity** that are past deadline. Note that some follow-up happens outside Spark (Slack, Linear, etc.), so flag gaps neutrally. ### Weekly Meeting Review For a broader view of meeting activity: 1. List this week's meetings: ```bash spark events --week ```
2. Check recent transcripts: ```bash spark meetings --filter "newer_than:7d" ```
3. Summarize: meetings attended, key decisions, outstanding follow-ups. ## Tips - Run `spark accounts` to discover available calendars before using `events --in`.
- Use `spark search` before meetings to find relevant email threads - it returns full bodies.
- Meeting transcripts include AI-generated summaries - start with just `spark meeting <id>` before pulling the full transcript.
- When scheduling, `availability` respects working hours (08:00-20:00) and skips weekends automatically.
- Combine transcript review with drafting follow-ups in a single flow for efficiency.
- Use `--filter "subject:standup"` on `meetings` to find recurring meeting transcripts.
- For the action item audit, meeting notes (`--notes`) often contain the clearest commitments. For recurring meetings, audit the last 2-3 sessions to spot items that carry over repeatedly.
