skills.description: Use this when programming or discussing lumbo-pelvic-femoral PRI - Left AIC AF/FA mechanics, Adduction/Extension Drop and Hruska lift tests, AF IR / AF ER goals, glute max / IC adductor / hamstring facilitation, or when Myokinematic is the correct course vs Pelvis Restoration (PADT gate).
skills.instructions:
# PRI Myokinematic Restoration (course skill) **Source (full text):** `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-myokinematic-restoration.txt` *(OCR from scanned PDF - cross-check coaching cues against clean reprints in Pelvis Restoration appendix when wording is noisy.)* **Course family:** Introductory course with Pelvis Restoration and Postural Respiration. --- ## 1. Core theory / asymmetry model (this course) Myokinematic Restoration owns **acetabulum-on-femur (AF) and femur-on-acetabulum (FA)** pathomechanics of the Left AIC pattern - how the pelvis orients the hip socket and how the femur orients in that socket across stance/swing. ### Stance / pattern definitions (manual)
- **Left stance in Left AF IR = Right AIC pattern** (desired alternating opposite) - **Right stance in Right AF IR = Left AIC pattern** (typical compensatory default) - **Right stance in Left AF ER = Left AIC pattern** (same family) **Desirable "real estate" for repositioning:** maximize **Left AF IR & Right AF ER** and motor control in that orientation. Left AF ER / Right AF IR is the patterned Left AIC state to leave. ### Why Left AIC dominates lumbo-pelvic-femoral findings
Same systemic asymmetry as other intros (right hemi-diaphragm + liver, right stance bias). Left pelvis anterior/forward → femur biomechanically oriented; psoas fails as femoral ER; VL and biceps femoris become antagonistic stabilizers (shared AIC description across manuals). Symptoms can present at knee, hip, groin, SI, back, shoulder blade, neck, face/TMJ with inability to fully adduct/extend/flex one or both sides and limited trunk rotation. ### Positional influences (themes from manual sections)
Patients stuck in **right AF IR + left AF ER** show characteristic length/strength imbalances:
- Posterior glute med (ER): long/weak secondary to adduction + IR - Anterior glute med (IR): long secondary to adduction but can be short/strong positionally - Hamstrings: proximal attachment more forward/elevated secondary to anterior innominate rotation → SLR looks "tight" while group is long, hypotonic, cortically suppressed - Right adductors / FA IRs overactive; femoral head can impinge anterior-medial acetabular cotyloid rim on FA ER secondary to right AF IR osseous position ### Soft tissue / capsule after repositioning
If capsular/soft-tissue issues remain after pelvic repositioning (over-compensatory activity):
- At 90° flexion, IR can be checked by superior ischiofemoral ligament and/or inferior capsule - At 90° flexion, ER can be checked by iliofemoral ligament and/or superior capsule Manual pairs stretches + AF/FA muscle strategies (IC adductor approximation, AF ER glute max, anterior/posterior glute med, obturator foramen control) by which rotation is limited left vs right. --- ## 2. Patterns to recognize ### Non-patho compensatory Left AIC (Myokinematic test results table)
| PRI test | Typical Left AIC result |
|---|---|
| Adduction Drop Test | + Left (unable to adduct left) |
| Extension Drop Test | often related findings; + L EDT with + L ADT relationships discussed |
| Straight Leg Raise | ↓ Left SLR |
| Trunk Rotation | Limited right trunk rotation (legs/rotation toward left limited in the patterned sense described) |
| FA ROM | ↓ Left FA IR ROM; ↓ Right FA ER ROM (vs opposite) |
| Hruska Adduction Lift | Level findings (often limited early levels on patterned side) |
| Hruska Abduction Lift | Level findings (e.g. Level 2 right noted in table OCR) | ### Functional relationships (manual shorthand)
- + L ADT with + L EDT relationships; − L EDT ↔ iliofemoral/pubofemoral laxity themes - Limited R trunk rotation vs non-limited (right iliolumbar laxity note) - ↓ L SLR = long, neuromuscularly weak, hypotonic, overly stretched "inactive" hamstring group - ↓ L FA IR ROM secondary to left AF ER osseous position - ↓ R FA ER ROM secondary to overactive right adductors/FA IRs + anterior-medial rim impingement in right AF IR - + R ADT with + L ADT → think **PEC** (hand off toward Pelvis / Postural Respiration) - L AF IR = R AF ER ↔ Right AIC (desired); R AF IR = L AF ER ↔ Left AIC (patterned) ### Femoral Acetabular ROM (seated) interpretation
Seated FA IR/ER with hips/knees ~90° (vs prone) to keep ligamentous site more resting. In non-pathologic compensatory Left AIC:
- ↓ L FA IR may reflect abducted left femur in L AF ER when legs face examiner → femur hits posterior-inferior acetabular rim on FA IR - ↓ R FA ER may reflect adducted right femur in R AF IR → femur "impinges" anterior-superior-medial acetabular rim on FA ER **After successful repositioning without osseous/capsular block:** expect ↑ L FA IR and ↑ R FA ER toward normal vs pre-repositioning. If still restricted → soft-tissue pathology pathway (not just "more stretching blindly"). ### FA neuromuscular control
Seated FA IR/ER strength; note **which muscle the patient feels on FA IR strength** (glute med vs TFL). TFL dominance = need repositioning / different facilitator strategy (manual testing note). --- ## 3. Assessment / special tests (this course) ### Core battery (evaluation form + test chapters)
1. **Adduction Drop Test (ADT)** - position / Left AIC flag 2. **Extension Drop Test (EDT)** - hip ligamentous laxity / extension pathomechanics 3. **Trunk Rotation** 4. **Straight Leg Raise (SLR)** 5. **FA IR / FA ER ROM** (goniometric, seated) 6. **FA IR / FA ER strength** (+ which muscle felt on IR) 7. **Hruska Adduction Lift Test** 8. **Hruska Abduction Lift Test** Evaluation form also lists Pelvis / Postural / Cervical / Advanced Integration blocks - Myokinematic sits first for AF/FA. ### ADT
Same sidelying procedure as other courses. Positive usually left in Left AIC; bilateral → PEC family. ### Hruska Adduction Lift Test (named for leg on examiner's shoulder)
Example: patient left sidelying, right ankle on examiner's shoulder → **Right** Hruska Adduction Lift. Position: back rounded; uppermost LE on shoulder (neutral hip, extended knee); lower leg flexed; pelvis neutral (no forward/back upper-pelvis rotation). Mechanics (stop at failed step): 1. Raise ankle of flexed lower leg to upper knee 2. Raise flexed lower knee while keeping ankle to knee 3. Raise lower hip maintaining above Grading themes: early failure ↔ FA ER weakness or AF stability failure of active extremity; higher levels demand IC adductor / obturator / pelvic diaphragm / oblique integration (OCR levels 1-5). ### Hruska Abduction Lift Test
Named for leg on wall (e.g. left sidelying, right foot on wall → Right test). Used as myokinematic measurement of muscle position, strength, timing. Steps (stop at failure): press bottom toes to wall → press bottom hip into surface (lower abs/adductors) → turn/raise bottom knee inward (IC adductor + anterior glute med) without top hip moving back → turn top heel up / toes down without dropping bottom knee → raise top leg off wall with trunk/hips stabilized. Also used in **Pelvis Restoration** algorithms as a progression gate (e.g. 3/5 before upright frontal-plane control). --- ## 4. Inhibit vs facilitate (Myokinematic composite) ### General AIC (Myokinematic column)
**Facilitate:** hamstrings, ischiocondylar adductor, gluteus maximus, anterior glute med/min, posterior glute med/min, IO/TA **Inhibit:** TFL, adductor magnus, psoas major, piriformis, vastus lateralis ### As related to Left AIC / Right BC / Right TMCC
**Facilitate:** L AF hamstrings, L AF IC adductor, R AF glute max, L FA anterior glute med/min, R FA posterior glute med/min, L IO/TA **Inhibit:** L TFL, R FA adductor magnus, L psoas major, L FA piriformis, R AF piriformis, R vastus lateralis Muscles that pull **femur into acetabulum** vs **acetabulum onto femur** are distinguished (glute max vs glute med/min themes) - AF IR work is not "more clamshells." --- ## 5. Repositioning logic and exercise progressions ### Course-selection gate (from Pelvis Identification page - critical)
After Left AIC repositioning attempt:
- **− L ADT / − L PADT → stay in Myokinematic Restoration Program** - **− L ADT / + L PADT → Pelvis Restoration Program** Bilateral:
- **− B ADT / − B PADT → Myokinematic + Postural Respiration** - **− B ADT / + B PADT → Pelvis Restoration** ### Left AIC repositioning menu (clean cues from Pelvis appendix reprint of Myokinematic techniques) **1. 90-90 Supported Hip Lift with Hemibridge** Feet on wall, hips/knees 90°. Exhale into pelvic tilt (tailbone slightly off; low back flat). Dig heels (not flat feet). Maintain tilt on left; straighten right; slowly on/off wall with breath - feel left posterior thigh. 3×10. Right sidelying, feet on wall, hips/knees 90°, ankles/knees together, back rounded. Bolster between feet; towel between knees; left knee lower than left hip/ankle. Push right foot into wall. Inhale - pull left leg back; exhale - squeeze left knee into towel 3s. Repeat 4-5 breaths, pulling further each inhale. ×5 sequences. **3. Left Sidelying Right Glute Max** Left sidelying, feet on wall, hips/knees 90°, back rounded. Towel under ankles and left abs. Press left hip down (right hip toward wall) - feel left abs. Shift right hip forward to slight stretch left outer hip. Turn right knee out using wall as fulcrum without right hip moving back - feel right outer hip. 4-5 breaths. ×5. ### Hierarchy themes (agenda: Left AIC Myokinematic Hierarchy; Femoroacetabular / AF IR programs)
Progress from repositioning → FA/AF ROM & strength restoration → Hruska lift level improvements → upright Left AF IR / Right AF ER integration (standing wall-supported left knee flexion with resisted right glute max; all-four right glute max; standing resisted patterns; lateral walking integration; right adductor magnus inhibition in hooklying; left posterior capsule inhibition standing; QL/psoas inhibition pairs). [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] ### Inhibition examples (appendix titles)
- Supine Hooklying Adductor Magnus Inhibition (right) - pelvic tilt + allow right knee to bolster; breathing holds - Left Posterior Capsule Inhibition - standing variants - Right QL and Left Psoas Inhibition - supine banded variants --- ## 6. What NOT to do / common errors - Do **not** stretch "tight hamstrings" as the primary fix when ↓ SLR reflects anterior innominate / long inhibited hamstrings. - Do **not** strengthen TFL-dominant FA IR - note which muscle is felt; reposition and facilitate glute med/IC adductor pathways. - Do **not** chase FA ER on the right with brute force while still in Right AF IR osseous position (rim impingement risk). - Do **not** keep someone in Myokinematic-only work when **PADT stays +** after − ADT - that is Pelvis Restoration. - Do **not** skip hemibridge / adductor pull-back / right glute max repositioning before advanced Hruska lift upright integration. - Do **not** interpret bilateral + ADT as "two unilateral Left AIC programs" only - PEC path. - Hruska lift compensations (flexing contralateral FA, pressing too hard into examiner's shoulder, lumbar extension instead of FA extension) invalidate the grade - coach the test, don't inflate the score. --- ## 7. How courses link | Need | Open |
|---|---|
| AF/FA Left AIC, ADT/EDT/SLR/Hruska lifts, AF IR real estate | **This skill** |
| Inlet/outlet, PADT/PART, Patho PEC, pelvic diaphragm | [Pelvis Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-pelvis-restoration) |
| ZOA, Right BC, PEC thorax, apical expansion, serratus/low trap | [Postural Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-postural-respiration) |
| Positional impingement / multi-directional instability after patterning | [Impingement & Instability](sand-workflow:pri-impingement-instability) | Myokinematic is the AF/FA foundation. Pelvis asks whether the pelvic diaphragm/inlet-outlet can hold what Myokinematic unlocks. Postural asks whether the thorax/ZOA can breathe in that pelvis. I&I asks what happens when neutrality is intermittent and joints start impinging or going multidirectionally unstable. --- ## 8. Achieve programming translation - Warm-up Left AIC: hemibridge → adductor pull-back → right glute max sidelying as indicated by ADT/SLR/FA ROM. - Retro stairs / standing Left AF IR wall drills when frontal-plane shift is the limiter. - Pair right-stance-biased athletes with left AF IR reference centers (left heel, left abs, left ischial seat, right arch). - If PADT + after ADT clears → switch programming reference to Pelvis skill. - OCR reference path is searchable for appendix exercise numbers when you need the exact non-manual title. Open the full reference text for complete hierarchy pages, FA soft-tissue tables, and evaluation form fields.

skills.name: pri-non-manual-techniques-workshop
skills.description: Use this when selecting primary PRI non-manual techniques, cueing reference/referent sensing, choosing position progressions, or deciding which muscle or inhibition family to open after Myokinematic, Pelvis, or Postural screens.
skills.instructions:
# PRI Primary Non-Manual Techniques Workshop **Sources (synthesized into one skill):**
- Typed notes (clean cues): `.../memory/reference/pri-nm-techniques-workshop-typed-notes.txt` - Feb 2023 workshop notes - Complete manual (structure/hierarchies): `.../memory/reference/pri-primary-nm-techniques-workshop-manual.txt` - *PRImary Non-Manual Techniques Workshop* complete manual Feb 2023 (© 2018-2023 PRI) **Extraction quality:** Both PDFs yielded searchable text via `pdftotext` (no OCR required). Manual is image-heavy for technique photos (positional outline pages are mostly figure plates); use typed notes for coaching cues and manual for program organization / reference-center theory. Prefer **non-manual** techniques in Achieve. This skill teaches when-to-use families, cueing, reference/referent logic, and neuro-motor order - not a full reprint of 300+ CD techniques. [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] --- ## 1. How PRI Non-Manual programs are organized Introductory courses each have Non-Manual CDs organized by **muscle, inhibition, and integration**, ordered by how you would isolate → inhibit → integrate. Integration program: 300+ techniques across nine positions; Integration symbol = thorax-pelvis via abdominals (**inhibit a pattern / facilitate a position** - not "strengthen abs"). **Reference centers (Integration):** left abdominals, left ischial seat, left heel, right arch. ### Terminology in titles
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Respiratory | Phase of respiration that expands L posterior mediastinum, L posterior outlet, or L posterior hip capsule |
| Reciprocal | Full available ROM both directions |
| Alternating | One side then the other (e.g. 3 breaths L then 3 R) |
| Supported | Proprioceptive surface (wall, floor foot, pillow, table) |
| Resisted | Band |
| Weighted | Free weight | ### Hard progression rules
- Neuro-motor position order follows Integration demand (exceptions: R Glute Max differs Myo vs Pelvis; Inhibition programs; R Low Trap/Tricep order on Postural CD). - **Bilateral inhibition always precedes unilateral.** - If a technique "looks in the wrong muscle folder," assume intentional facilitation via inhibitory muscle/position/process - don't reshuffle by bodybuilding logic. - Example: 90-90 Supported Hip Lift with Hemibridge **always** precedes 90-90 Hip Lift with Balloon. ### Why BC muscle order is R LT/Tricep → L LT/Serratus → R Serratus → R Subscap
Typical L AIC + R BC: pelvis/spine/diaphragm oriented right; thorax rotates back left above diaphragm for frontal balance and R reach. Right-handedness promotes that left upper rotation and disadvantages R low trap / triceps / serratus. 1. **R low trap + tricep** - retract/posterior-tilt scapula; stabilize spine with L abs; elbow extension; thoracic flexion; lat down. 2. **L low trap + L serratus** - reorient upper thorax; stabilize upper quadrants during R reach. 3. **R serratus** - stabilize R scapula for R reach **without** needing left upper trunk rotation. 4. **R subscap** - HG IR independent of overactive lat (after neutrality). Later positions in each muscle set demand **more isolation with more substitution inhibition**. --- ## 2. Position decision-making (advantages) | Position | Best for |
|---|---|
| Supine | Bilateral sensory comparison; ANS outcomes (SLR); cranial-pelvis sagittal tilt; early facilitation |
| Sidelying | Best **non-dominant unilateral compensatory inhibition** |
| All Four | Flexed appendage co-activation during thoraco-abdominal flexion; best respiratory position |
| Short Seated | Best passive reposition |
| Long Seated | Best desirable position to strive for and maintain |
| Seated | Thoracic-pelvis rotation without thoracic-cervical hyperactivity |
| Standing | Re-biasing alternating lateralized cortical / centering sense |
| Prone | Inhibit L TFL via L FA IR |
| Kneeling | L glute med isolation with hamstrings shortened | --- ## 3. Course positional outlines (families to open) ### Myokinematic Restoration (examples of muscle folders) ### Pelvis Restoration ### Postural Respiration Open the matching course skill for test gates (ADT/PADT, apical, etc.) before picking a folder. --- ## 4. Workshop technique cards (from typed notes - Achieve-usable) Each card: **Reference / Referent(s)** → inhibit → who it's for → coaching notes. - **Ref:** L post calcaneus/heel (low). **Referents:** L IO/TA (high), R med long arch (low). - **Inhibit:** R thoracic diaphragm (by empowering left); L post outlet / L ant inlet / R post inlet / R ant outlet; L posterior ground with R forward movement; L rearfoot with L abs + R forefoot (late double stance → left shift). - **For:** difficulty rotating upper trunk R while lower trunk left; need left "load" to free R arm/chest (static/overtight right). - **Cues:** Push L hand into floor → R trunk rotation with L AF IR (L IO/TA). Sense leftward retro. Lower upper body to floor before going vertical. Also inhibits L short FA ERs, R short AF IRs, R short back rotators (R QL, R IO/TA). - **Ref:** L ischial seat (mod), R med long arch (low). **Referents:** R lat post upper chest (R LT/triceps), L ant AF capsule (L adductor), L IO/TA, R post hip (R glute max). - **Inhibit:** Overuse R IO/TA/EO + R rectus; R BC; R hip flexor (psoas+TFL); TF ERs; R intercostals. - **For:** sense of left / shift left; R thoracic curve; R mouse/computer; R shoulder impingement; interscap pain / flat backs; limited R cervical lateral flexion; post R subclavius release. - **Cues:** L HG ER (teres minor/infraspinatus) helps posterior mediastinal expansion and forces R apical up; cross-ref anterior rib abs with posterior scapular stabilizers + SA. ### Stair Short Seated Balloon
- **Ref:** L ischial seat. **Referents:** L IO/TA, L post calcaneal tuberosity, R med long arch, L post mediastinum, R lat post upper chest. - **Inhibit:** R hemilateral foot/ischial/ZOA "grounding"; lat / longissimus / interscap; quads. - **For:** unsteady left foot / can't pause without leaning back-right; wide BOS gait; can't squat from short quads/hip flexors. - **Cues:** Best position to establish posterior mediastinums **and** upper lateral chest expansion on inhale **and** exhale; prep for retro / cranio activity. ### Long Seated Press Down
- **Ref:** R lat post upper chest (R LT/tricep) R>L; L post heel L>R. **Referent:** L IO/TA L>R. - **Inhibit:** Hip and neck flexors via hamstring-tricep cross-reference. - **For:** protracted shoulders + deep lumbar curve; periscapular weakness; bicipital tendinitis; sitters who overwork rectus + anterior chest/neck. - **Cues:** Awareness of 90° SLR with neutral thoracic orientation; balance mid/lower trap, SA, rhomboids, subscap with tricep; enhances subscap/SA with abs + dorsiflexion. - **Ref:** L ischial tuberosity. **Referents:** R LT/tricep, L ant AF capsule (adductor), L IO/TA, R med long arch. - **Inhibit:** R IO/TA; R upper trap; R scalenes/BC; R intercostals; L TFL; patterned inlet/outlet set; R posterior mediastinum; L levator. - **For:** poor R overhead reach sitting/standing; can't reach up/out while turning upper body same side. - **Cues:** Sense L adductors + L glute med/min during L posterior mediastinum + R apical expansion; pelvic/hip anchor for contralateral release. - **A ref:** L heel; referents R glute max, L IO/TA, L post mediastinum. - **B ref:** R heel; referents L glute max, R LT/tricep, L post mediastinum. - **Inhibit:** A = L AIC/R BC; B = L low-back extension + L LT/triceps. - **For:** dissociation issues; poor ground friction sense + scapula-on-thorax friction; flat back / flat affect / rigid. - **Cues:** Alternating secures LE for ipsilateral lower torso rotation + contralateral upper torso rotation **without** cervical help; intro to retro; both pictures get L posterior mediastinum (A via L SA + L hammies; B via R SA + left leg lift). - **Ref:** L ischial tuberosity. **Referents:** L IO/TA, R glute max. - **Inhibit:** L TFL; R hip adductors; L rectus femoris. - **For:** poor L single-leg strength (step overs/throughs); flat L feet / don't know how to pronate. - **Mods:** Ball between knees → more ant glute med/min; bolster under R ankle → more R FA ER vs abd; light weight on L ankle → more L glute demand. ### Left Sidelying Supported Trunk Lift
- **Ref:** L IO/TA, L heel. **Referent:** R LT/triceps. - **Inhibit:** R calcaneus; R ischial seat; L canines / R molars; L post hip; L LT/triceps (+ R bicep/pec); R ant AF capsule; R IO/TA. - **For:** vestibular leftward figure-8 difficulty; Superior T4; L hemidiaphragm weakness/SOB; clenchers; post MMOO/MOOO orthotic. - **Cues:** Pillow under pelvis aligns pelvis-cranial bowls; wall anchors feet for torso-pelvis-cranium axis. ### Seated Resisted Reciprocal Pull Downs
- Keep upper trunk turned right. A emphasize inhale; B emphasize exhale. - **Inhibit:** A = L upper trap / L apical / R BC; B = R upper trap / R abs / L anterior BC. - **For:** retrain alternating trunk with L pelvis/hip security; cervicalgia / temporal-frontal HA. - Lower chair → more heel / ischial / ST / OA extension R>L demand. ### Single Leg Stance with Contralateral Glute Max
- Block under foot = hemi vestibular-postural demand; pole in R hand for balance / compression bias. - **Inhibit:** A = back extensors esp R QL/paravertebrals; B = L pec minor. - **For:** A LBP / weak quads / overused L VL; B L AIC reposition / weak L FA IRs in hip extension. ### Standing Supported Bilateral IO/TA
- **Inhibit:** glossopharyngeal, tongue, shoulder elevators, upper traps, lats, plantarflexors. - **For:** forward head; sleep apnea; laryngeal tension; swallowing issues. - **Cues:** Retro BOS sense; Functional Squat Test ≥3 allows abs to rotate torso; arms overhead with eccentric hammies/adductors; intro R then L arm reach. ### Standing Left Knee Flexion with Right AIC Progression
- **Inhibit:** latero-spatial single-leg transfer sense; hip flexors; R quads. - **For:** SLR >90° bilaterally (abs as rotators, hammies stabilize); LBP/SI; limited L shoulder flexion (pulls L thorax under L scapula); R tennis elbow from over-supination; R quad overuse. - Ground sense lifts on **left** secondary to R UE extension position. ### Standing Supported Left Glute Push
- Valsalva-like between exhale and inhale without balloon/nose pinch; lift R LE → R psoas + R FA ER to keep mass left. - **Inhibit:** anterior neck / scalenes / accessory respirators. - **For:** autonomic dysfunction / dysautonomia (see PRI Breathing Mechanics in COVID Times week 3 handout referenced in notes). ### Modified Two Point Gait with Left AF IR
- Poles slow pelvis timing vs scapular alternation; R pole lever with R triceps → R LT + pelvic floor for L AF IR cognition. - **Inhibit:** ipsilateral UE-LE ambulatory pattern (R UE with R LE / L with L). - **For:** ataxia; scissor gait. - **Inhibit:** L hip flexors; R SCM; R BC (pecs); R hip adductors; L trunk rotation / R IO/TA. - **For:** R PF pain / quad tendinitis; R LE centering during L hip adduction; bilateral lat / back-over-extension users. - Mimics resisted decline retro walk (L abs; R floor back / R foot forward during L hip extension). --- ## 5. When to open which family (coach decision map) | Goal / finding | Start family |
|---|---|
| Need ZOA / L AIC inhibition / balloon | 90-90 family, Stair Short Seated Balloon, Wall Supported Squat Balloon |
| Need L AF IR + R freedom | R Sidelying L Adductor Pull Back; Seated Respiratory L AF IR + intercostal pulley |
| Need R apical + shift left | L Sidelying Foot Toward Ceiling + R glute max / R apical |
| Need PEC / paraspinal down | Stair Short Seated Balloon; Standing Supported Bilateral IO/TA; Paraspinal inhibition folder; Functional Squat families |
| Need true R HG IR | R Subscap folder **after** neutrality (not lat IR) | Always re-test course screens after a technique block. --- ## 6. What NOT to do - Cherry-pick "cool" late positions (prone/standing isolations) before early ones work. - Unilateral inhibition before bilateral. - Cue techniques as ab hypertrophy or generic mobility. - Ignore reference/referent sensing - without tactile co-reference the neuro outcome weakens. - Skip course test gates and jump folders by symptom name alone ("shoulder" → random serratus). --- ## 7. Achieve programming translation - Warm-up: 1-2 repositioning techniques from the map (often 90-90 balloon or stair short seated balloon + one sidelying). - Tertiary: match folder to remaining test (R LT/tricep vs L serratus vs inhibition). - Write **reference sense** in athlete cues ("left heel + left abs," "right arch," "left sit bone"). - Keep clinician manuals (Superior T4, Subclavius, Infraclavicular) out of gym improvisation - see Right BC guidelines skill. Open course skills for theory depth; open this skill for technique selection and cueing.

# PRI Pelvis Restoration (course skill) **Source (full text):** `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-pelvis-restoration.txt` **Course family:** Introductory course alongside Myokinematic Restoration and Postural Respiration. Expert reference for Achieve programming and intelligent discussion. Not a license to diagnose or perform manual pelvic techniques. --- ## 1. Core theory / asymmetry model (this course) Pelvis Restoration reframes the Left AIC / PEC problem in **pelvic inlet and outlet** language and ties the **pelvic diaphragm** to the respiratory diaphragm (reciprocal and alternating goals). ### Left AIC pelvic position summary (manual)
- **LEFT:** Inlet IP ER = IS IR = Outlet IsP IR = AF ER - **RIGHT:** Inlet IP IR = IS ER = Outlet IsP ER = AF IR (Translation for coaches: left hemi-pelvis is stuck in the pattern that blocks left AF IR / left frontal-plane shift; right side is the stance-biased opposite.) ### Neuro-muscular facilitation goals - to inhibit a Left AIC (inlet/outlet map) **Pelvic Inlet**
| Side | Action | Key muscles (manual colors/labels) |
|---|---|---|
| Left | IP IR anterior inlet (Ext/Add/IR) | IO/TA |
| Right | IP ER anterior inlet (Flex/Abd/ER) | Rectus femoris, sartorius |
| Left | IS ER posterior inlet | Iliacus, gluteus medius |
| Right | IS IR posterior inlet | Gluteus maximus (superior fibers) | **Pelvic Outlet**
| Side | Action | Key muscles |
|---|---|---|
| Left | IsP ER anterior outlet (Flex/Abd/ER) | Hamstring, IC adductor, obturator, iliococcygeus |
| Right | SI IR posterior outlet | Gluteus maximus (inferior fibers), piriformis, coccygeus | ### PEC pattern summary
- **Pelvic inlet:** Bilateral IP ER / IS IR - anterior sacrum flexed - **Pelvic outlet:** Bilateral IsP IR - posterior sacrum extended; coccyx flexed - Pelvic diaphragm **positionally descended, hypertonic, inflexible** Manual axiom: **"Behind every PEC is a Left AIC pattern."** ### Patho PEC position summary
Same bilateral inlet/outlet directional description as PEC, but pelvic diaphragm is **descended, bulged, and high resting tone** - a more pathologic pelvic-floor / outlet presentation. Patho-specific tests are bolded in the test matrix (below). ### Respiratory influence themes (course sections)
- Left AIC: hemi-diaphragm / hemi-pelvis coupling; left posterior outlet mediastinum expansion matters - PEC: bilateral anterior rib flare/ER; bilateral posterior mediastinum restriction - Patho PEC: same extension bias with greater pelvic diaphragm dysfunction [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] --- ## 2. Patterns to recognize ### Left AIC (pelvis course)
+ Left ADT; often + Left PADT; + Right PART; Standing Reach > 0"; Functional Squat < 3/5; Hruska Abduction Lift < 3/5. Person cannot shift into left AF IR / control left outlet abduction and right outlet adduction in gait terms. ### PEC
+ Bilateral ADT; + Bilateral PADT; Standing Reach > 0"; PART − bilateral; Functional Squat < 3/5; Hruska Abd Lift < 3/5. Bilateral anterior inlet / posterior outlet bias; pelvic diaphragm descended/hypertonic. ### Patho PEC (* patho tests bolded in manual)
+ Bilateral ADT; **Standing Reach = 0"**; + Bilateral PADT; **PART + bilateral or unilateral**; **Functional Squat > 3/5**; Hruska Abd Lift < 3/5. Reach may look "better" while PART/squat pathology flags pelvic diaphragm / pathologic PEC. ### Ilio-sacral (IS) instability (Left AIC patients)
Separate hierarchy in the manual when IS instability overlays Left AIC - do not skip to aggressive alternating activity before inlet/outlet inhibition sequencing. --- ## 3. Assessment / special tests ### Battery (Pelvis Restoration Tests)
1. **Adduction Drop Test (ADT)** - Position 2. **Standing Reach Test (SRT)** - Sagittal plane 3. **Pelvic Ascension Drop Test (PADT)** - Frontal plane stance phase 4. **Passive Abduction Raise Test (PART)** - Frontal plane swing phase 5. **Functional Squat Test** 6. **Hruska Abduction Lift Test** - also a Myokinematic measurement with pelvic interpretation [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] ### ADT (detail)
Same sidelying procedure as other courses. Positive = femur will not adduct; reflective of osseous restriction from acetabular labral rim / related structures; usually left in Left AIC; bilateral in PEC/Patho PEC. ### Test matrices (when ADT is + left or bilateral) **Left AIC**
| Test | Finding |
|---|---|
| ADT | + left |
| Standing Reach | > 0" |
| PADT | + left |
| PART | + right |
| Functional Squat | < 3/5 |
| Hruska Abd Lift | < 3/5 | **PEC**
| Test | Finding |
|---|---|
| ADT | + bilateral |
| Standing Reach | > 0" |
| PADT | + bilateral |
| PART | − bilateral |
| Functional Squat | < 3/5 |
| Hruska Abd Lift | < 3/5 | **Patho PEC**
| Test | Finding |
|---|---|
| ADT | + bilateral |
| *Standing Reach | 0" |
| PADT | + bilateral |
| *PART | + bilateral or unilateral |
| *Functional Squat | > 3/5 |
| Hruska Abd Lift | < 3/5 | ### Critical course-selection gates (PRI Identification page) Decision:
- **− L ADT / + L PADT → Pelvis Restoration Program** - **− L ADT / − L PADT → Myokinematic Restoration Program** [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] Decision:
- **− B ADT / + B PADT → Pelvis Restoration Program** - **− B ADT / − B PADT → Myokinematic Restoration and Postural Respiration Program** This is the clearest "which course owns this athlete today" rule in the three intros. --- ## 4. Inhibit vs facilitate (Pelvis composite) From composite-of-courses tables (also printed in Postural manual): **Pelvis Restoration - AIC chain (general)** - Facilitate **Pelvic Inlet:** proximal iliacus, sartorius, rectus femoris, IO/TA - Inhibit **Pelvic Inlet:** thoracic diaphragm, IO/EO, paravertebrals - Facilitate **Pelvic Outlet:** proximal obturator, iliococcygeus, puborectalis, pubococcygeus, glute max, piriformis, coccygeus - Inhibit **Pelvic Outlet:** adductor magnus, hamstrings **As related to Left AIC** (sided): Facilitate inlet L proximal iliacus, R sartorius, R rectus femoris, L IO/TA; outlet L proximal obturator, L iliococcygeus, L puborectalis/pubococcygeus, R glute max, R piriformis, R coccygeus. Inhibit inlet R thoracic hemi-diaphragm, R IO/EO, L paravertebrals; outlet R adductor magnus, R hamstrings, L piriformis, L coccygeus, L glute max. **Goals language:** turn patterns from Left AIC "ON/OFF" maps toward **Right AIC alternating** (reciprocal and alternating pelvic and respiratory diaphragms). For PEC/Patho PEC, goals emphasize facilitation of abs with posterior pelvic tilt and proximal adductors into reciprocal inlet IP IR / outlet IsP ER bilaterally. --- ## 5. Repositioning logic, algorithms, hierarchies ### Left AIC Pattern - Pelvis Restoration Algorithm (test results cluster) **Repositioning menu**
1. 90-90 Supported Hip Lift with Hemibridge 3. Left Sidelying Right Glute Max **Branches**
- Repositions to **− L ADT, − L PADT, − R PART** → further assessment if still can't hold; may need other PRI courses - Remains **all tests +** or **− L ADT but + L PADT and/or + R PART** → **Pelvis Restoration Program** (maximize hemi 90-90 position) - Then when **− PADT** and **3/5 Hruska Abd Lift**: upright L single-leg frontal plane static/dynamic control (left outlet abduction) → upright R single-leg frontal plane (right outlet adduction) → sidelying frontal plane integration → seated left pelvic outlet ascension control → reciprocal alternating activity If unable to reposition pelvis: re-evaluate techniques or assessment tests from other PRI courses (manual). ### Left AIC Pelvis Restoration Hierarchy (when − L ADT and + L PADT and/or + R PART) **Facilitation (Alternating) Program - sequenced:**
1. Turn **on right anterior pelvic inlet via IP ER** (rectus femoris + right sartorius) 2. Turn **on left anterior pelvic outlet via IsP ER** (left puborectalis/pubococcygeus) with left inlet IP IR; turn on left iliococcygeus and left obturator via left adductors 3. (continues in manual - inhibit right posterior inlet via IP ER to promote right inlet abduction; upright left single-leg frontal plane control; sidelying frontal plane integration; etc.) **Inhibition (Alternating) Program - sequenced themes from manual:**
1. Inhibition sequencing paired with the above 2. Inhibit right posterior inlet via IP ER to promote right inlet abduction 3. Upright left single-leg frontal plane control (left outlet abduction via left iliacus and left …) 4. Sidelying frontal plane integration (left inlet adduction and right inlet abduction with left …) Appendix inhibition families (non-manual titles to know): ### PEC Pattern - Pelvis Restoration Hierarchy
Gate: **− Bilateral ADT and (+ …)** per manual hierarchy page. Algorithm page pairs with PEC repositioning techniques and then PEC-specific facilitation/inhibition (abs + posterior pelvic tilt + proximal adductors; bilateral inlet/outlet goals). ### Pathologic PEC Pattern - Hierarchy / Algorithm
Gate: **− Bilateral ADT** with Patho test cluster. Emphasizes pelvic diaphragm / floor isolation considerations (appendix: treatment considerations for isolation of pelvic floor and transverse …). Higher caution; not a "just breathe harder" problem. ### Ilio-Sacral (IS) Instability Treatment Hierarchy for Left AIC patients
Separate ladder - address IS instability sequencing before assuming standard alternating gait integration will stick. ### Left AIC / PEC / Patho PEC repositioning technique lists (appendix) [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] ### Squat & respiration (appendix - Bilateral Anterior Inlet / Posterior Outlet section)
Manual includes dedicated squat ascend/descend respiratory coaching in the pelvis inhibition appendix (pair with Postural Respiration squat-breathing logic). In all variations, squat **ascend** is exhalation-biased to keep ribs down / extensors quiet. --- ## 6. What NOT to do / common errors - Do **not** send someone to Myokinematic-only work when **− ADT / + PADT** - that is **Pelvis Restoration**. - Do **not** send someone to Pelvis-only work when **− ADT / − PADT** - that is **Myokinematic** (and for bilateral −/−, Myokinematic **+ Postural Respiration**). - Do **not** treat PEC as "two Left AICs" without bilateral test logic and bilateral inlet/outlet goals. - Do **not** miss Patho PEC: Standing Reach of **0"** with **+ PART** and **Functional Squat > 3/5** is not a win - it is a different bucket. - Do **not** skip repositioning into hemi 90-90 neutrality before upright single-leg frontal-plane drills. - Do **not** jump to reciprocal alternating activity before inlet/outlet facilitation-inhibition hierarchy and PADT resolution. - Do **not** ignore IS instability hierarchy in Left AIC patients who keep losing neutrality. - S&C should not improvise manual IP ER / IsP IR / pelvic floor techniques - keep non-manual menus. --- ## 7. How courses link | Finding after repositioning attempt | Open |
|---|---|
| − L ADT / − L PADT | [Myokinematic Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-myokinematic-restoration) |
| − L ADT / + L PADT | **This course** |
| − B ADT / − B PADT | Myokinematic **and** [Postural Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-postural-respiration) |
| − B ADT / + B PADT | **This course** (PEC/Patho path) |
| Thorax/BC/apical/ZOA remain limited after pelvis neutrality | Postural Respiration |
| Scapular-thoracic / HG IR / impingement remain after BC tests − | [Impingement & Instability](sand-workflow:pri-impingement-instability) | Pelvis Restoration sits between raw AF/FA myokinematics and thoraco-abdominal respiration: it owns **whether the pelvic diaphragm and inlet/outlet can alternate** so ZOA and AF IR can stick. --- ## 8. Achieve programming translation - Choose breathing/repositioning from the **correct course gate** (PADT/PART vs ADT alone). - Left AIC pelvis days: hemibridge / adductor pull-back / right glute max sidelying family → then frontal-plane single-leg control. - PEC days: wall-supported reach, 90-90 in passive FA IR with balloon, modified all-four belly lift - bilateral extension bias first. - Patho PEC flags → collaborate clinically; don't "progress squat depth" off a 0" reach with + PART. - Keep reference centers in coaching: left abs, left ischial seat, left heel, right arch (Integration language shared across intros). Open the full reference for full hierarchy steps, manual technique pages, and Hruska Adduction Lift appendix notes.

skills.name: pri-postural-respiration
skills.description: Use this when programming or discussing thoraco-abdominal PRI - Zone of Apposition, Left AIC / Right BC / PEC recognition, apical expansion, serratus and low-trap progressions, lat/intercostal/paraspinal inhibition, or how Postural Respiration links to Myokinematic, Pelvis, and Impingement & Instability.
skills.instructions:
# PRI Postural Respiration (course skill) **Source (full text):** `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-postural-respiration.txt` **Course family:** One of three introductory courses (with Myokinematic Restoration and Pelvis Restoration). Impingement & Instability is the secondary course that extends Right BC / scapular-thoracic logic. This skill is for expert-level discussion and Achieve programming decisions. It does **not** replace formal PRI coursework or clinical diagnosis. Prefer non-manual techniques in S&C; manual techniques are listed only so you understand clinician pathways. --- ## 1. Core theory / asymmetry model (this course) ### Why the thorax is patterned
Humans are inherently asymmetrical: larger/stronger right hemi-diaphragm, liver on the right (better positions the right diaphragm), no liver on the left → tendency to relax the left abdominal wall. Early development biases shift/rotation of the spine to the right. Right extremity dominance and daily right weight-shift reinforce this. The pattern **most often prevalent** (manual Section: Left AIC pattern):
- **Left Anterior Interior Chain (Left AIC)**
- **Right Brachial Chain (Right BC)**
- **Right posterior back muscles (PEC contribution)** Left pelvis anteriorly tipped and forwardly rotated → directional rotational influence on low back/spine to the right → compulsive compensatory movement in trunk, UEs, and cervical-cranial-mandibular musculature. **Greatest impact is on rib alignment and position → breathing.** Common objective findings secondary to trying to stay balanced over that unlevel pelvis (manual):
- Elevated anterior ribs on the left
- Lowered/depressed shoulder and chest on the right
- Posterior rib hump on the right
- Overdeveloped lower right back muscle
- Spinal curvature; head/face asymmetry
- One shoulder lower; continual shift of body to one side through the hips
- Difficulty adducting/extending/flexing legs one or both sides; limited trunk rotation one or both ways; limited apical expansion one or both sides; cervical rotation / mandibular / shoulder flexion / horizontal abduction / IR limitations Respiratory dysfunction (e.g. asthma) and occupational/repetitive positions can also drive compensatory left anterior/forward pelvis. ### Polyarticular chains (Postural Respiration definitions) **Anterior Interior Chain (AIC)** Two AIC tracts (L and R). Attachments from costal cartilage/bone of ribs 7-12 to lateral patella, fibular head, lateral tibial condyle. Core members: **diaphragm + psoas**, with iliacus, TFL, biceps femoris, vastus lateralis. Influence respiration, trunk/ribcage/spine rotation, and LE position. Suboptimal AIC mechanics (manual AIC section):
1. Diaphragm pulls dorsal (thoracic) spine up and forward 2. Psoas + iliacus pull lumbar spine and pelvis down and forward 3. Combined → increased lumbar lordosis (hemi-lordosis), anterior pelvic tilt, active lumbar extension / hyperinflation 4. Diaphragm becomes more tonic/postural → less effective as a respiratory muscle; thorax form/function challenged 5. Posterior mediastinal expansion often restricted 6. Ilium anterior + forward → femur oriented inward; psoas fails as femoral ER; VL and biceps femoris become antagonistic hip stabilizers **Brachial Chain (BC)** Two BC tracts over anterior pleural/cervical area. Influence cervical rotation, shoulder dynamics, apical inspiratory expansion. Attach from costal cartilages/bone of ribs 4-7 and xiphoid to occipital bone, mandible, coracoid. Members: **triangularis sterni, SCM, scalenes, pec minor, intercostals, pharynx/anterior neck**. - Right BC opposed by right PEC, lower trap, serratus, external rib rotators, **plus left internal obliques** - Left BC opposed by left PEC, lower trap, serratus, external rib rotators, **plus right internal obliques** **Posterior Exterior Chain (PEC)** Posterior extensors / QL system that closes the posterior mediastinum and drives bilateral extension bias when both sides are "on." ### Zone of Apposition (ZOA) - central concept of this course
ZOA = cylindrical portion of diaphragm apposed to inner aspect of lower rib cage (from costal insertion up to costophrenic angle where fibers leave the rib cage to form the free dome). In standing quiet breathing ≈ **¼-⅓ of total rib cage surface**; at rest overall ≈ **~30%**. Controlled by abdomen/obliques; directs diaphragmatic tension. Rib cage and abdomen are always mechanically coupled through ZOA. - Elevated anterior, externally rotated ribs → **decreased ZOA** (uni- or bilateral) depending on pattern, abdominal weakness, and use - Chronic hyperinflation changes diaphragm dimensions **exclusively in the ZOA** (manual cites) - Loss of ipsilateral/bilateral abdominal opposition → hyperinflation, paradoxical breathing, accessory overuse **ZOA restoration logic (Hruska):** Apposition lost almost always on the **left** (→ Left AIC) or **bilaterally** (→ PEC). IO/TA primarily responsible for ipsilateral diaphragm leaflet opposition and ipsilateral lower rib opposition on inspiration → contralateral apical expansion (esp. in trunk rotation/gait). Active established ZOA example: successful **standing reach (fingers to toes)** while inhaling with **anterior mediastinal compression + posterior mediastinal expansion**. Passive ZOA via PRI manual techniques if active ZOA unobtainable. Maximum ZOA (passive, supine): end-exhale trans-diaphragmatic strength strongest in thoraco-lumbar flexion, weakest in extension. Reference centers emphasized on Integration techniques (CD notes): **left abdominals, left ischial seat, left heel, right arch**. ### Posterior mediastinum (Right BC context)
Mnemonic **DATES**: Descending aorta, Azygous/hemiazygous, Thoracic duct, Esophagus, Sympathetic trunk. Bounded by pericardium (ant), diaphragm (inf), transverse thoracic plane T4 (sup), vertebral column (post), pleura (lat). - Unlocks transverse plane when **opened (flexed)**; limits thoracic rotation when **closed (extended)** in PEC - In Right BC: more **closed/anterior on the left**, more **opened/posterior on the right** --- ## 2. Patterns to recognize (with this course's lens) ### Left AIC (thoraco-abdominal expression)
Left hemi-pelvis anterior/forward; mass/orientation to the right; left ZOA lost; left anterior ribs elevated; airflow often easier into left upper chest with compensatory strategies. Compels Right BC above the diaphragm to keep the person facing forward. ### Right BC
Compensatory upper thorax/rib cage orientation (often described as thorax rotating back toward left above diaphragm for frontal-plane balance and right UE reach). Right low trap, triceps, serratus lose normal scapular retraction / spinal stabilization / rib IR-ER roles because of right-handed activity + left upper trunk rotation. Manual Right BC upright scapular pattern cues (visual): forward rib cage with possible rib hump; humeral IR in the patterned position can drive **posterior-superior humeral glenoid impingement** (link to Impingement & Instability). ### Bilateral PEC
Bilateral extension / hyperinflation expression. Bilateral limitations on key tests (below). Posterior mediastinum closed; stiff/rigid back; limited bilateral arm swing; limited apical expansion one or both sides. ### Combined Left AIC / Right BC / Right TMCC
Composite tables in the manual treat these as the typical coupled system. Cervical Revolution covers Right TMCC in depth; Postural Respiration still expects you to know the thorax piece couples into cervical-cranial patterns. --- ## 3. Assessment / special tests and what positives mean ### AIC tests (* = key)
1. *Adduction Drop Test 2. Extension Drop Test 3. *Trunk Rotation 4. *Apical Expansion **AIC opposition muscles:** hamstrings, glutes, IO/TA. ### BC tests (* = key)
1. *Apical Expansion 2. *Shoulder Horizontal Abduction 3. Trunk Rotation 4. *Posterior Mediastinum Respiratory Reach Test 5. Humeral Glenoid Internal Rotation 6. Shoulder Flexion 7. Cervical Axial Rotation **BC opposition muscles:** triceps, lower trapezius, abdominal obliques, TA, serratus anterior. ### PEC tests (* = key)
1. *Trunk Rotation (bilateral limitation) 2. *Adduction Drop Test (bilateral limitation) 3. *Extension Drop Test (bilateral limitation) 4. Apical Expansion 5. Posterior Mediastinum Respiratory Reach Test **PEC opposition:** abdominal obliques. ### Adduction Drop Test (procedure + meaning)
Sidelying, bottom hip/knee flexed ~90°. Passively flex-abduct-extend top hip to neutral keeping ~90° knee flexion; stabilize pelvis so it does not fall back / allow femoral IR. Top innominate directly over bottom (too cephalad → false +; too caudal → false −). **Positive:** femur will not adduct (restriction from anterior-inferior acetabular labral rim, transverse ligament, piriformis, or posterior-inferior femoral neck on posterior-inferior acetabular rim) - often secondary to anteriorly rotated, forward hemipelvis. **Usually left in Left AIC.** ### Standing reach / active ZOA screen
Inability to touch toes with posterior expansion on inhale = ZOA / extension-bias problem (ties to PEC and hyperinflation). Successful toe touch **with** anterior compression + posterior expansion on inhale ≈ active ZOA. ### Right BC treatment-guideline test cluster (appendix)
Track as positive/negative:
- Left horizontal abduction - Left cervical axial rotation - Left humeral glenoid flexion - Right apical expansion - Right humeral glenoid IR --- ## 4. Inhibit vs facilitate (composite tables from the manual) ### Postural Respiration course focus (general chain table)
| Chain | Facilitate (position) | Inhibit |
|---|---|---|
| AIC | Thoracic diaphragm | Psoas major |
| BC | Lower trap, middle trap, triceps, triangularis sterni, serratus anterior | Pec major (HG adductors), pec minor (scapulothoracic IR), latissimus dorsi |
| PEC | IO/TA, external obliques | Paravertebrals, quadratus lumborum | ### As related to Left AIC / Right BC / B PEC
| Chain | Facilitate | Inhibit |
|---|---|---|
| L AIC | L thoracic hemi-diaphragm | L psoas major |
| R BC | R lower trap, R triceps, L triangularis sterni, B serratus, B middle trap | L HG adductors (pec major), R scapulothoracic IR (pec minor), R lat |
| B PEC | L IO/TA, R external obliques | B paravertebrals, R QL | ### Cross-course composite (know what other courses own)
**Myokinematic (L AIC / AF-FA):** facilitate L AF hamstrings, L AF IC adductor, R AF glute max, L FA ant glute med/min, R FA post glute med/min, L IO/TA; inhibit L TFL, R FA adductor magnus, L psoas, L FA piriformis, R AF piriformis, R VL. **Pelvis (inlet/outlet language):** facilitate pelvic inlet (L proximal iliacus, R sartorius, R rectus femoris, L IO/TA) and outlet (L proximal obturator, L iliococcygeus, L puborectalis/pubococcygeus, R glute max, R piriformis, R coccygeus); inhibit inlet (R thoracic hemi-diaphragm, R IO/EO, L paravertebrals) and outlet (R adductor magnus, R hamstrings, L piriformis, L coccygeus, L glute max) - per Left AIC-related table. --- ## 5. Repositioning logic and non-manual progressions ### Order philosophy (PRI Non-Manual CD organization - Postural Respiration)
Typical L AIC + R BC involves pelvic/spinal/diaphragmatic orientation toward the right with thorax rotating back left above the diaphragm. Right-handed activity promotes that left upper trunk rotation and disadvantages R low trap / triceps / serratus. **Neuromotor order for this course's muscle programs:**
1. **Right low trap + right tricep** - retract/posterior-tilt scapula; lower spinal rotation left; promote thoracic flexion; deactivate lats 2. **Left low trap + left serratus** - mid-spinal rotation right; stabilize thorax for right thoracic rotation and left rib IR; serratus lower fibers ER ribs / upper fibers IR ribs; promote desired kyphosis; engage serratus via arms reaching forward **and** ribs moving back 3. **Right serratus** - stabilize right scapula for right arm reach **without** left trunk rotation / right rib retraction 4. **Right subscapularis** - true HG IR independent of lat (after neutrality) **Position progressions (neuro-motor demand increases):** - R low trap/tricep: Supine → All Four → Seated → Long Seated → Standing → Sidelying → Prone - L serratus: Supine → Sidelying → Seated → Standing → All Four - L low trap: Supine → All Four → Seated → Standing → Sidelying - R serratus: Supine → Sidelying → Seated → Long Seated → Standing → All Four - R subscap: Supine → Sidelying → Seated → Prone → Standing Use these **after** repositioning with a non-manual or manual technique. Later positions demand more isolation with greater inhibition of substitutions. **Inhibition program rule:** bilateral inhibition precedes unilateral. Terminology: *Respiratory* = expands left posterior mediastinum / left posterior outlet / left posterior capsule; *Reciprocal* = full ROM both directions; *Alternating* = one side then the other; *Supported* / *Resisted* / *Weighted* as defined in CD notes. ### Key AIC non-manual techniques (* from appendix overview)
1. 90-90 Hip Lift 2. 90-90 Hip Lift with Hip Shift 3. 90-90 Hip Lift with Medial Hamstring 4. 90-90 Supported Hip Lift with Hemibridge 5. **90-90 Hip Lift with Balloon** ### Key PEC non-manual techniques
1. Stair Short Seated Balloon 2. Paraspinal Release with Left Hamstring 3. Standing Wall Supported Resisted Reach ### ZOA abdominal / Postural Respiration repositioning family ### Right BC PRI treatment guidelines (decision tree - handout p.47 + appendix overview)
**Dedicated deep skill:** [PRI Right BC Treatment Guidelines](sand-workflow:pri-right-bc-treatment-guidelines). Summary here for course context. [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] After ZOA abdominal non-manual techniques:
- **Some/all tests still +** → Left AIC + Sternal with Active Pelvic Tilt **manual** (clinician); if still +, **Right Superior T4 manual**; then: - All tests − → stabilize with **Left Low Trap & Left Serratus** *(handout: prior to initiating R LT/tricep)* - 90-90 supported wall leg lift with alternating resisted arm reach; seated resisted serratus punch with L hammies; standing serratus squat; all four belly lift reach; three point stance. - Still + **and** − R apical / + L apical → **Right Subclavius manual** (Superior T4 syndrome) → then L low trap/L serratus when clear.
- **+ cluster with − R HG IR (≤80° or better)** → PRI Left AIC + Right BC manuals to thorax neutrality → then **R subscapularis**.
- All tests − **and** sufficient R ST function (can reach in supine/prone/left sidelying without tests returning +) → **Standing** R low trap / R tricep. ### Inhibition menus (when to use) **Right BC inhibition considerations** if: limited R apical expansion; limited L shoulder horizontal abduction; difficulty with deep inspiration without compensation (L ribs flare, L back extends, R SCM, lateralize body right); ongoing tension R upper trap / SCM / QL / lat / paraspinals / hip flexors. Techniques include:
- Sidelying Swiss Ball Inhibition - R Sidelying R Apical Expansion with Balloon - R Sidelying R Apical Expansion with L FA IR - Standing QL and Intercostal Stretch - Late Left AIC Stance with Right Arm Reach - All Four Intercostal and Latissimus Inhibition - L Sidelying L Flexed FA Adduction with R Glute Max and R Trunk Rotation **PEC inhibition considerations** if: limited apical expansion one/both sides; forward locomotion without rib rotation (stiff back); asymmetrical/limited bilateral arm swing. Techniques include:
- Dorsal Thoracic Inhibition - All Four Belly Lift Walk - Stair Short Seated Balloon - Paraspinal Release with Left Hamstrings - Squatting Bar Reach - Standing Wall Supported Resisted Reach - Heel Stair Descents --- ## 6. What NOT to do / common errors - Do **not** load heavy sagittal strength on a flared, extended, ZOA-less thorax and call breathing "done." - Do **not** chase "weak serratus" or "tight shoulder" before asking what the **ribcage under the scapula** is doing (winging often = rib position). - Do **not** train true HG IR via lat-dominated patterns when Right BC / lat is the problem - restore thorax neutrality then train **subscapularis**. - Do **not** skip the neuromotor order (R low trap/tricep before L low trap/serratus before R serratus before R subscap) without a reason. - Do **not** use late-position progressions (sidelying/prone standing variants) before the person can demonstrate the acquired action with less inhibitory demand. - Do **not** treat bilateral PEC like unilateral Left AIC only - need bilateral ADT/EDT/trunk rotation logic and paravertebral/reach-based inhibition. - Manual Superior T4 / Subclavius / Infraclavicular pathways are clinician tools; S&C should not improvise them. - CD note: if a technique seems "in the wrong muscle program," assume intentional neuromotor design - don't reshuffle by bodybuilding logic. --- ## 7. How this course links to the others | Course | Owns | Hand-off cues |
|---|---|---|
| **Myokinematic Restoration** | Lumbo-pelvic-femoral AF/FA mechanics, Left AIC LE tests (ADT, etc.), AF IR | Pelvis ID page: **− L ADT / − L PADT → Myokinematic program**; − B ADT / − B PADT → Myokinematic **and** Postural Respiration |
| **Pelvis Restoration** | Pubo-sacral inlet/outlet, PADT/PART, Patho PEC, pelvic floor integration | **− L ADT / + L PADT → Pelvis program**; − B ADT / + B PADT → Pelvis |
| **Postural Respiration (this)** | ZOA, BC, PEC thorax, apical expansion, serratus/low trap/subscap, lat/intercostal/paraspinal inhibition | Feeds I&I when scapular-thoracic capacity fails despite − BC tests |
| **Impingement & Instability** | When neutrality exists but R ST function/IR/impingement mechanics remain | Manual treatment guidelines explicitly route "insufficient right scapular-thoracic function" to I&I-minded BC manuals + R serratus/subscap | **Integration symbol** on Non-Manual CDs marks techniques that integrate thorax with pelvis via abdominals - **not** to "strengthen abs," but to inhibit a pattern and facilitate a position. --- ## 8. Achieve programming translation (S&C) - Early session: ZOA/repositioning (90-90 balloon family, wall-supported reach, sidelying adductor/glute patterns as indicated). - Swimmers / overhead: bias lat inhibition, serratus + subscap, wall reach / squat-reach, avoid feeding bilateral PEC extension. - Pair extension-biased strength with flexion/reach or exhalation-biased breathing check. - Gate "earned" inhale-on-descent squat breathing until ZOA is demonstrated. - Use test language in coach notes (ADT, apical expansion, trunk rotation, HG IR) without claiming clinical diagnosis. Open the full reference text for coaching scripts, case studies (Right BC & PEC), and sequential breathing notes.

skills.name: pri-right-bc-treatment-guidelines
skills.description: Use this when interpreting Right BC test clusters and deciding whether to progress Right low trap/tricep vs Left low trap/serratus vs Right serratus vs Right subscapularis, including Superior T4 / Subclavius / Infraclavicular clinician pathways and inhibition menus after ZOA work.
skills.instructions:
# PRI Right BC Treatment Guidelines (handout skill) **Primary source:** `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-right-bc-treatment-guidelines.txt` *(Postural Respiration handout p.47 - Right BC PRI Treatment Guidelines, © 2000-2013 PRI)* **Companion overview (fuller decision tree with I&I / R serratus / R subscap branches):** `.../pri-right-bc-treatment-guidelines-overview-appendix.txt` (from Postural Respiration appendix) and the full course extract `pri-postural-respiration.txt`. This skill is the **operational decision tree** for Right BC after ZOA work. Prefer non-manual techniques in Achieve S&C. Manual Superior T4 / Subclavius / Infraclavicular / Sibson / Intercostal paths are listed so you understand **clinician** pathways - do not improvise them in the gym. Cross-links: [PRI Postural Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-postural-respiration) · [PRI Impingement and Instability](sand-workflow:pri-impingement-instability) · [PRI breathing exercise selection](sand-workflow:pri-breathing-exercise-selection) · [PRI Non-Manual Techniques Workshop](sand-workflow:pri-non-manual-techniques-workshop) --- ## 1. Test cluster (track + / −) Before and after every stage, recheck this Right BC cluster: | Test | Typical patterned finding |
|---|---|
| Left horizontal abduction | + (limited) |
| Left cervical axial rotation | + (limited) |
| Left humeral glenoid flexion | + (limited) |
| Right apical expansion | + (limited) *or* − R / + L in Superior T4 syndrome branch |
| Right humeral glenoid internal rotation | + (limited) *or* − (≤80° or better) when routing to R subscap | **Coach translation:** these are screening language for warm-up / tertiary choices - not a clinical diagnosis. Pair with ADT / trunk rotation / standing reach (ZOA) from course skills. --- ## 2. Always start: ZOA Abdominal Non-Manual Techniques Handout entry box - restore Zone of Apposition / abdominal opposition **before** scapular muscle programs: 1. **90-90 Hip Lift with Right Arm Reach and Balloon**
2. **PRI Wall Supported Squat with Balloon**
3. **Left Sidelying Knee Toward Knee with Balloon** Achieve equivalents often used in warm-up: 90-90 balloon family, wall-supported squat/reach with balloon or long exhale, left sidelying knee-to-knee / adductor patterns, right apical expansion sidelying with left reach + left adductor sense. **Gate:** do not progress R low trap / tricep isolation while the athlete is still flared, extended, and failing apical / horizontal abduction screens without first earning ZOA. --- ## 3. Decision tree (handout + appendix overview) ### Branch A - All tests − after ZOA NM
→ **Right Low Trap & Right Tricep Program** (primary neuromotor next step when thorax/BC tests clear). ### Branch B - All or some tests remain + after ZOA NM
→ **Clinician path:** Left AIC and Sternal - With Active Pelvic Tilt **manual** techniques. → If still +: **Right Superior T4 Manual Technique**. → Then recheck: #### B1 - All tests − after Superior T4 path #### B2 - All or some tests remain + **and** − Right Apical Expansion / + Left Apical Expansion
→ **Right Subclavius Manual Technique** (Superior T4 syndrome path - clinician). → When all tests − → **Left Low Trap & Left Serratus** (stabilize), then later R low trap/tricep as indicated. ### Branch C - Impingement & Instability consideration (appendix overview)
**All tests −** but **insufficient right scapular-thoracic function** (reach forward drops R shoulder or IR's R UE; or prone R serratus weaker):
→ Then **Right Serratus Anterior** program. ### Branch D - Cluster still + but **− Right HG IR** (≤80° or better available)
→ Clinician: PRI Left AIC + Right BC manuals to thorax neutrality → Then **Right Subscapularis** program (true HG IR independent of lat). ### Branch E - All tests − **and** sufficient R ST function
Patient can reach forward with R UE in supine, prone, and left sidelying with tests remaining − --- ## 4. Muscle program menus (from handout) ### Right Low Trap & Right Tricep Program (examples listed)
- Supine Weighted Tricep Curls - Supine Resisted Right Tricep Extension with Right HG IR - Long Seated Supported Press Down with Abdominals - Paraspinal Release with Left Hamstring - Sidelying Trunk Lift (Right) **Acquired action (Postural / NM workshop):** R low trap + tricep retract and posterior-tilt scapula on a stabilized spine with left abs; promote thoracic flexion; deactivate lat dominance. **Position progression (neuro-motor demand ↑):** Supine → All Four → Seated → Long Seated → Standing → Sidelying → Prone. ### Left Low Trap & Left Serratus Anterior Program (stabilize spine - handout says prior to R LT/Tricep when coming off manuals)
- Standing Serratus Squat - All Four Belly Lift Reach - Three Point Stance **Acquired action:** L low trap = mid-spinal rotator to the right; L serratus stabilizes thorax for right thoracic rotation / left rib IR and desired kyphosis (reach arms forward **and** ribs back). ### Right Serratus Anterior (I&I / ST insufficiency branch)
Use after neutrality + clinician infraclavicular-family work when R ST strength/position still fails. Goal: stabilize R scapula for R arm reach **without** left trunk rotation / right rib retraction compensation. ### Right Subscapularis (− R HG IR branch)
Only after thorax neutrality. Train true HG IR **independent of lat** - critical for swimmers and overhead athletes (link I&I). --- ## 5. Clinician-only pathways (know, don't coach as gym drills) | Manual | Role in tree |
|---|---|
| L AIC + Sternal with active pelvic tilt | Persistently + tests after ZOA NM |
| Right Subclavius | − R apical / + L apical after Superior T4 (Sup T4 syndrome) | S&C response when athlete is stuck on these branches: keep ZOA / inhibition / earlier NM programs, refer to PRI-trained clinician, do **not** load cuff isolation on a patterned thorax. --- ## 6. Inhibition menus (when BC stays sticky) Use when: limited R apical expansion; limited L horizontal abduction; deep inspiration drives L rib flare / L back extension / R SCM / right lateralize; chronic R upper trap / SCM / QL / lat / paraspinal / hip-flexor tension. Examples from Postural Respiration inhibition logic (coach-usable):
- Sidelying Swiss Ball Inhibition - R Sidelying R Apical Expansion with Balloon (± L FA IR) - Standing QL and Intercostal Stretch - Late Left AIC Stance with Right Arm Reach - All Four Intercostal and Latissimus Inhibition - L Sidelying L Flexed FA Adduction with R Glute Max and R Trunk Rotation --- ## 7. What NOT to do - Skip ZOA abdominal NM and jump to R low trap curls / band pull-aparts. - Train "weak serratus" or "tight shoulder" before ribcage under the scapula is addressed. - Use lat-dominated IR / pull patterns when the goal is R subscap. - Start standing / sidelying / prone R LT-tricep variants before supine/all-four versions succeed. - Improvise Superior T4 / Subclavius / Infraclavicular techniques in S&C. - Treat I&I ST failure the same as "all tests +" - different branch (R serratus after clinician ST manuals). --- ## 8. Achieve programming translation 1. Screen: L horiz abd, L cervical rot, L HG flex, R apical, R HG IR + ADT / reach. 2. Warm-up: ZOA list (balloon 90-90, wall squat balloon, sidelying apical + adductor). 3. If screens clear → R low trap / tricep family (start supine/seated). 4. If screens sticky → more inhibition + L serratus / L low trap stabilize; escalate clinician if manuals indicated. 5. Swimmers / OH: bias lat inhibition, wall reach / all-four belly lift reach, then R serratus / R subscap only after neutrality language. 6. Pair extension-heavy lifts with flexion/reach or exhalation-biased breathing check. Open [PRI Postural Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-postural-respiration) for ZOA theory; [PRI Impingement and Instability](sand-workflow:pri-impingement-instability) when ST function fails despite − BC tests.

skills.name: pri-shoulder-pain-prescription
skills.description: Use when prescribing PRI non-manual techniques for overhead right bicipital tendonitis or right shoulder impingement (Advanced Integration menus with Left IO/TA), including mechanic lists and named technique banks.
skills.instructions:
# PRI shoulder pain prescription (overhead) **Source:** PRI *Advanced Integration* pp. 196-199 - *Overhead Shoulder Instability and Tendonitis*. Full cleaned text: `/home/box/agent-data/agents/e9d0fc7f-22cc-4b14-80a6-4b8361108e36/memory/reference/pri-shoulder-pain-prescription.txt` [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] This skill owns the **overhead athlete right bicipital tendonitis vs right impingement mechanic lists and technique menus** (with Left IO/TA). It does not replace I&I course theory or full swim dryland. --- ## Always frame first **Most common overhead problems:** bicipital tendonitis · shoulder impingement **Most common reason:** COM does not shift adequately over the stance / contralateral leg as the **thorax abducts under the side** the shoulder is flexing into. Fix the patterned trunk-rib-scap problem; don’t only chase local cuff. Keep **Left IO/TA** in the game on every menu below. --- ## Right bicipital tendonitis - mechanics 1. ↓ Trunk / chest-wall rotation **to the right**
2. ↓ Rib **external rotation** (front ribs up + rib-cage retract, usually **right**) during L IO/TA co-contraction - weak serratus / forward shoulder. Prefer **\*** techniques.
3. Lat overuse as humeral **IR** engine because scap position kills subscap + serratus Muscle map: serratus · subscap · lat (not “more lat pull”). ### Technique menu (Right bicipital + L IO/TA) | # | Technique | Catalog |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | Supine Resisted Right HG IR with Left HG ER | R LT & R Tricep Supine #16 |
| 11 | Reversed “C” Push-Ups | Integration Supine #35 | **\* priority** when rib ER / R trunk / serratus themes dominate (mechanics #2). **Programming bias:** R apical / R trunk rotation · serratus punch family · R HG IR **without** lat dominance · lat hang then R LT/tricep ownership. --- ## Right shoulder impingement - mechanics 1. Poor rib-cage expansion with diaphragmatic breathing 2. Poor abs **co-contract on inhale** (keep ZOA while expanding) 3. Lat over-activity controlling scap via thoracic **extension** → scap posterior tilt + downward rotation 4. Weak **R low trap + long head of triceps** → winging + anterior tilt of scapula Also → intra-scapular weakness. Muscle map: traps · triceps. ### Technique menu (Right impingement + L IO/TA) | # | Technique | Catalog |
|---|---|---| **Programming bias:** R LT + R triceps as primary drivers · abs stay on inhale · lat inhibition / press-downs · AF belly lift + paraspinal release for extension bias · not more vertical pull volume that feeds lat. --- ## Quick decision tree 1. Overhead pain → classify **bicipital** vs **impingement** (can coexist; pick the dominant mechanic list). 2. Confirm L IO/TA + COM / thorax-abduction story before loading cuff isolation. 3. Bicipital → \* serratus / R trunk / R HG IR menu. Impingement → R LT/tricep + abs-on-inhale menu. 4. Swimmers: also open swim-dryland + PRI swimming; this PDF is the named technique bank. 5. Neutrality / Right BC gates still come from Postural Respiration / Right BC guidelines / I&I - this skill is the **prescription sheet**, not the full course. ## Anti-patterns
- More lat-driven IR or heavy pull volume for “shoulder stability”
- Band pull-aparts only while thorax still can’t expand or rotate right
- Ignoring L IO/TA when dosing R LT / R tricep / serratus drills

skills.name: pri-squat-and-respiration
skills.description: Use this when coaching squat ascent/descent breathing variants, deciding when inhale-on-descent is earned via ZOA, or applying Left AIC / PEC pelvic-rib positioning to loaded squats.
skills.instructions:
# PRI The Squat and Respiration **Source:** `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-squat-and-respiration.txt` Lori Thomsen, MPT, PRC - *The Squat and Respiration* (Pelvis Restoration handout, © 2010-2013 PRI). [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] This skill tells you **how to breathe through squat descent and ascent** based on ZOA capacity, Left AIC vs PEC positioning, and load. It does not replace formal PRI coursework. --- ## 1. Pattern review that drives squat breathing ### Left AIC (speak left side; right is opposite)
- Left anterior ribs **ER**, posterior ribs **IR** → left central diaphragm descended; left posterior mediastinum shortened.
- Anterior pelvic **inlet** forwardly rotated, ER, abducted (IP ER = AF ER); anterior **outlet** IR / adducted (IsP IR = AF ER).
- Left anterior pelvic floor (puborectalis/pubococcygeus) descended; posterior outlet shortened/tight (glute max, piriformis, coccygeus).
- **Anterior chest wall + anterior pelvic outlet = INHALATION position** (abs and anterior inlet lengthened). - **Posterior pelvic outlet = EXHALATION position** (muscles shortened).
- Pelvic inlet integrates respiratory + pelvic diaphragms through **left IO/TA**. ### PEC (bilateral version of the above)
- Bilateral anterior ribs ER / posterior IR → bilateral descended central tendons; bilateral posterior mediastinums restrictive on inhale.
- Bilateral anterior inlet forward/ER/abd; anterior outlets IR/add → bilateral anterior floor descended, posterior outlets taut.
- Bilateral anterior chest + anterior outlet = inhalation position; posterior outlets = exhalation position.
- Inlet integration via IO/TA gives thoracic + pelvic diaphragms **power**. **Squat setup implication:** - Left AIC → seek pelvic position of **L inlet IP IR / outlet IsP ER = L AF IR**. - PEC → slight **posterior pelvic tilt** so bilateral inlet IP IR / outlet IsP ER. --- ## 2. Squat descent - three breathing variants (easiest → hardest) Order is based on ability to **find and maintain ZOA** (outer abdominal control through IO/TA). ### Variant 1 - Partial exhale down, finish exhale up
**Who:** decreased abdominal strength with ZOA; **or** lifting under heavy load (powerlifting / strength & conditioning). **Why it works:** Partial exhale on descent drives anterior ribs (L in Left AIC; bilateral in PEC) into **IR**. Coupled with correct pelvic position, respiratory and pelvic diaphragms **ascend** → internal support of body weight and control of air/pressure/organs under load. **Achieve cue:** Soft partial exhale as you sit; complete the exhale as you stand. Do not dump into full Valsalva extension. ### Variant 2 - Exhale down, hold 1-3 breaths at bottom, exhale up
**Who:** decreased abs / hard to maintain ZOA; needs **posterior mediastinum and outlet expansion**; inhales into extension. **Caution:** May be too challenging for heavy Olympic-style barbell squats. **Why it works:** Exhale on descent again IR's anterior ribs and integrates thorax-pelvis. Holding the squat 1-3 breaths is a **PRI process under load**: each inhale in the bottom with maintained anterior rib IR + pelvis position maximizes posterior mediastinum and pelvic outlet expansion. Athlete neurologically learns to **inhale without going into extension** in the squat. **Achieve cue:** Exhale to the hole → breathe 1-3 cycles keeping ribs down / abs on → exhale to stand. Extension breathers / PEC-Right BC athletes often live here before earning Variant 3. ### Variant 3 - Inhale down, exhale up (PRI goal)
**Who:** already has abdominal strength **with appropriate ZOA**, but needs synchronization of respiratory and pelvic diaphragms. Extremely challenging under heavy load - **earn it**. **Why it works:** Inhale on descent with abs/ZOA holding anterior rib IR + correct pelvis expands posterior mediastinum and outlet while diaphragms stay ascended → internal support **and** maximal power to push (quads, hamstrings, glutes, abs). **Achieve cue:** Only after toe-touch / standing reach with posterior expansion on inhale (active ZOA), and after Variants 1-2 are clean. Never default heavy athletes here on day one. --- ## 3. Squat ascent - always exhale In **all three** variants, ascend on **exhale**. - Exhaling out of the squat pulls left ribs down with IO/TA as L IP IR / IsP ER / AF IR occurs.
- PEC athletes maintain respiratory + pelvic floor **ascension**.
- Exhalation with rib IR = concentric IO/TA → best **paravertebral inhibition** → optimal thorax/pelvis to push.
- **Inhaling while standing up** descends respiratory and pelvic diaphragms and can create pathology / poor power optimization (Thomsen). **Hard rule for Achieve:** do not coach "breathe in and drive up" on patterned or ZOA-poor athletes. --- ## 4. PEC / Right BC implications for loading | Finding | Loading / breathing bias |
|---|---|
| Weak abs / no ZOA / heavy load | Variant 1 |
| Extension breather, PEC, limited posterior expansion | Variant 2 (pause breathes in hole) |
| Established ZOA, needs diaphragm sync | Variant 3 |
| Right BC / lat-dominant swimmer or OH athlete | Pair squat with reach / wall-supported reach; prefer exhale-biased variants until apical + horiz abd improve - see Right BC guidelines |
| Flared ribs, heels up, can't toe-touch | Do not load deep squat as primary; ZOA reposition first | Heavy extension-biased strength without exhalation-biased or pause-breath work feeds PEC. --- ## 5. What NOT to do - Default inhale-on-descent for everyone "because powerlifting Instagram." - Ascend on inhale. - Chase depth/load before anterior rib IR and pelvic AF IR language exist. - Treat Variant 2 pause as a rest break - it is ZOA training under load. - Ignore PEC bilateral setup (needs slight posterior tilt language, not only left AF IR). --- ## 6. Achieve programming translation - Warm-up: ZOA (90-90 balloon, wall squat balloon) then choose squat breath variant from screens. - Strength block: write the breath variant in the Direction line (e.g. "partial exhale down / full exhale up"). - Progress 1 → 2 → 3 only when ZOA holds. - After squat sessions, recheck toe-touch / SLR / apical - success isn't only bar weight. - Cross-check Right BC tree if upper thorax tests stay + despite good squat breathing. Open the breathing index for day-of picks; open Postural / Pelvis course skills for ZOA and inlet-outlet theory.

skills.name: pri-swimming-in-depth
skills.description: Use this when applying a PRI lens to swimming pattern, stroke pathomechanics, lat/BC/PEC themes, and dryland implications for freestyle, fly, back, or breast - separate from pool turn/start ISO angles and Achieve stroke dryland playbook.
skills.instructions:
# PRI Swimming: An In-Depth Look (Berge) **Source:** `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-swimming-in-depth-look.txt` **Separate skills (do not merge):**
- [Swim turn and start ISO angles](sand-workflow:swim-turn-and-start-iso-angles) - pool-transfer isometric joint angles
- [Swim dryland programming](sand-workflow:swim-dryland-programming) - Achieve stroke/start/turn/UW dryland rules, volume bias, shoulder menus
- This skill - **PRI pattern / pathomechanics** lens [REDACTED paragraph: custom_skill_person_names_unsure] --- ## 1. Why swimming patterns differently Unique demands (Berge):
- UE-primary propulsion; highly technique-dependent; high drag → streamlining (max shoulder flexion/abduction).
- Mostly **prone** → encourages spinal extension; buoyancy reduces gravity "corrections."
- Extreme repetition (e.g. ~14,400 arm pulls/week at 6k yd × 6 with ~10 strokes/25 yd).
- Breath pattern: mouth inhale, prolonged hold / nasal exhale under water - often carried onto land as dysfunctional breath-holding / hyperinflation vs nose-in / mouth-out diaphragmatic norms. **Injury profile:** shoulder impingement / cuff-biceps tendinopathy / instability most common (disabling shoulder pain reported ~27-87% competitive); also low back and knees. --- ## 2. Acquired pattern = PEC + underlying Left AIC / Right BC ### Sport-driven PEC / hyperinflation
- Deep low back (erectors); elevated anterior ribs / flares - Forward rounded shoulders (pecs + lats on extended spine / hyperinflated ribs) - Forward head; anterior pelvic tilt (back + kick-driven hip flexors) - Hyperextended knees on land ### Muscle imbalance package
- Strong, short **lats** → limit rib expansion / trunk rotation; drive lumbar extension - Strong **pecs** → long weak intrascapulars; restrict rib depression - Strong hip flexors / back extensors from flutter-dolphin + prone posture - Long inefficient **IO/TA** for rib/pelvis stability and rotation - Diaphragm poorly positioned (ribs up front, pelvis/hip flexors down back) → accessory neck/back breathing → limited cervical rotation ### Asymmetry still applies
Left AIC / Right BC make reciprocal trunk/neck rotation and rib expansion side-biased → often: unilateral breath preference, asymmetric catch/reach/recovery, limited backstroke shoulder turn, shoulder impingement. --- ## 3. General needs for all swimmers (program goals) 1. Balanced airflow / chest wall motion all directions 2. Hamstring + abdominal strength to oppose PEC extension 3. Glutes, **lower traps, triceps, serratus, subscapularis** opposing pull-dominant lat/pec pattern 4. Efficient, well-positioned diaphragm 5. Flexibility: hip flexors, back extensors, lats, pecs, neck, shoulder ERs **Order:** achieve/maintain **neutral posture with trunk flexion + thoracic rotation + abs + breathing** *before* chasing isolated cuff/scap work. Patterned ribs put scapulae in the wrong place - cuff work on a bad thorax fails. --- ## 4. Stroke-specific PRI management ### Freestyle (most training mileage)
**Pathomechanics:** Impingement early pull-through or early recovery from humeral "hyperextension" (humerus behind scapular axis) when scapula is anterior/down-rotated from pec-lat dominance; limited body roll worsens depth or high-elbow recovery. EMG: weak **serratus** and **subscap** correlate with ipsilateral impingement; lat/pec power not different painful vs non-painful. **PRI rationale:** R BC / PEC extension limits thoracic flexion and ST congruence → scapula rides forward/up (upper trap/pec); serratus length-tension fails; lat + IR'd scapula force posterior cuff ER compensation and **inhibit subscap** so lat becomes the IR engine → anterior pain. Limited L trunk/cervical rotation biases **right-side breathing** (easier for typical Right BC). **Management focus:**
